label: Qn:main
title: Question
body_md:
\label{Qn:main}
Under which conditions on $P$ and $X$ is exactness or nuclearity of the C*-algebra of a Fock covariant representation induced by exactness or nuclear embeddability of $A$?
head: environment

label: Qn:main2
title: Question
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $P$ be a unital subsemigroup of an amenable discrete group $G$ and let $X$ be a product system over $P$.
Let $t$ be an equivariant representation of $X$.
Then $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$ is exact if and only if $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},t_\ast}$ is exact for every ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$.
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
Let $P$ be a unital subsemigroup of an amenable discrete group $G$ and let $X$ be a product system over $P$.
Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item ${\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)$ is exact.
\item $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$ is exact for an injective Fock covariant representation $t$ of $X$. 
\item $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, t_\ast}$ is exact for an injective Fock covariant representation $t$ of $X$, for all ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$. 
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $P$ be a unital subsemigroup of an amenable discrete group $G$ and let $X$ be a product system over $P$.
Let $t$ be an equivariant representation of $X$.
Then $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$ is nuclear if and only if $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},t_\ast}$ is nuclearly embedded in $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$ for every ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$.
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $P$ be a unital finitely aligned subsemigroup of an exact discrete group $G$ and let $X$ be a compactly aligned saturated product system over $P$ with coefficient C*-algebra $A$.
Then ${\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)$ is exact if and only if $A$ is exact.

Suppose in addition that $G$ is amenable, and $t$ is an injective Fock covariant representation of $X$.
Then $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$ is exact if and only if $A$ is exact.
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $P$ be a unital strongly finitely aligned subsemigroup of an amenable discrete group $G$ and let $X$ be a compactly aligned saturated product system over $P$ with coefficient C*-algebra $A$.
Let $t$ be an injective equivariant Fock covariant representation of $X$.
Then $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$ is nuclear if and only if the embedding $A \hookrightarrow [\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$ is nuclear.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let ${\mathcal{A}}$ be a C*-algebra. 
We say that ${\mathcal{A}}$ is \emph{exact} if for any C*-algebra ${\mathcal{B}}$ and any ideal ${\mathcal{I}} \lhd {\mathcal{B}}$ the sequence
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
0 \arrow[r] & {\mathcal{A}} \otimes {\mathcal{I}} \arrow[r] & {\mathcal{A}} \otimes {\mathcal{B}} \arrow[r] & {\mathcal{A}} \otimes ({\mathcal{B}}/{\mathcal{I}}) \arrow[r] & 0
\end{tikzcd}
\]
is short exact.
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
\cite{Kir91, Kir94, Kir95}
Let ${\mathcal{A}}$ be a C*-algebra. 
Then ${\mathcal{A}}$ is exact if and only if there exist a faithful $*$-representation $\pi \colon {\mathcal{A}} \to {\mathcal{B}}(H)$ and nets of completely contractive completely positive maps $\phi_\lambda \colon {\mathcal{A}} \to M_{k_\lambda}(\mathbb{C})$ and $\psi_\lambda \colon M_{k_\lambda}(\mathbb{C}) \to {\mathcal{B}}(H)$ such that 
\[
\lim_\lambda \| \psi_\lambda \circ \phi_\lambda (a) - \pi(a) \| = 0 \text{ for all } a\in {\mathcal{A}}.
\]

title: Proof
body_md:
The implication [(i) $\Rightarrow$ (iv)] is \cite[Exercise 3.9.8]{BO08}.
We provide a proof to show how Proposition~\ref{P:localsplit} is used.
Suppose that ${\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}}$ and ${\mathcal{J}}$ are exact and that the short exact sequence is locally split. 
Let ${\mathcal{I}}$ be an ideal in a C*-algebra ${\mathcal{B}}$ and denote by $q'\colon {\mathcal{B}} \to {\mathcal{B}}/{\mathcal{I}}$ the quotient map. 
Consider the following commutative diagram
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
& 0 \arrow[d] 
& 0 \arrow[d] 
& 0 \arrow[d] 
& \\
0 \arrow[r] 
& {\mathcal{J}}\otimes {\mathcal{I}} \arrow[r] \arrow[d] 
& {\mathcal{J}}\otimes {\mathcal{B}} \arrow[r] \arrow[d] 
& {\mathcal{J}}\otimes ({\mathcal{B}}/{\mathcal{I}}) \arrow[r] \arrow[d] 
& 0 \\
0 \arrow[r] 
& {\mathcal{A}}\otimes {\mathcal{I}} \arrow[r] \arrow[d] 
& {\mathcal{A}}\otimes {\mathcal{B}} \arrow[r] \arrow[d] 
& {\mathcal{A}}\otimes ({\mathcal{B}}/{\mathcal{I}}) \arrow[d] \\
0 \arrow[r] 
& ({\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}})\otimes {\mathcal{I}} \arrow[r] \arrow[d] 
& ({\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}})\otimes {\mathcal{B}} \arrow[r] \arrow[d] 
& ({\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}})\otimes ({\mathcal{B}}/{\mathcal{I}}) \arrow[r] \arrow[d] 
& 0 \\
& 0
& 0
& 0
&
\end{tikzcd}
\]
where exactness of the top and bottom rows follows from exactness of the C*-algebras ${\mathcal{J}}$ and ${\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}}$, respectively, and exactness of the columns follows from Proposition~\ref{P:localsplit}. 
We have to show that the middle row is also exact. 

To that end, let $x$ be in $\ker({\operatorname{id}}_{\mathcal{A}}\otimes q')$ and we will show that $x\in {\mathcal{A}}\otimes {\mathcal{I}}$. 
By commutativity of the diagram and exactness of the bottom row we obtain 
\[
(q\otimes {\operatorname{id}}_{\mathcal{B}})(x) \in ({\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}})\otimes {\mathcal{I}},
\]
hence we may pick $y\in {\mathcal{A}}\otimes {\mathcal{I}}$ such that $(q\otimes {\operatorname{id}}_{\mathcal{I}}) (y)= (q\otimes {\operatorname{id}}_{\mathcal{B}})(x)$. 
Set $z:= x-y$ and note that $(q\otimes {\operatorname{id}}_{\mathcal{B}}) (z)=0$. 
In particular, by exactness of the middle column we obtain that $z\in {\mathcal{J}}\otimes {\mathcal{B}}$. 
Since $z\in \ker({\operatorname{id}}_{\mathcal{A}} \otimes q')$, exactness of the top row implies that $z\in {\mathcal{J}} \otimes {\mathcal{I}} \subseteq {\mathcal{A}} \otimes {\mathcal{I}}$.
We conclude that 
\[
x= x-y+y=z+y \in {\mathcal{A}} \otimes {\mathcal{I}},
\]
as required.

The equivalence [(iii) $\Leftrightarrow$ (iv)] is the version proven in \cite[Theorem 10.2.4]{BO08} if one follows verbatim the proofs for finite-dimensional operator subsystems and completely contractive completely positive maps.

The implication [(iii) $\Rightarrow$ (ii)] is a standard trick exhibited in the comments prior to \cite[Proposition C.2]{BO08}.
Namely, if for a finite-dimensional unital operator system $E \subseteq {\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}}$ there is a completely contractive completely positive map $\theta\colon E \to {\mathcal{A}}$ such that $q \circ \theta = {\operatorname{id}}_E$, then let $\omega \colon E \to \mathbb{C}$ be a unital completely positive map and replace $\theta$ by $\theta + (1_{\mathcal{A}} -\theta(1_{{\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}}}))\omega$.

For the implication [(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i)] let $E \subseteq {\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}}$ be a finite-dimensional operator space and apply the hypothesis for the unital operator system $E'$ generated by $E$ to obtain a unital completely positive map $\theta'\colon E' \to {\mathcal{A}}$ such that $q \circ \theta' = {\operatorname{id}}_{E'}$.
Then the completely contractive restriction map $\theta := \theta'|_E$ is the required local lift.

title: Proof
body_md:
The implication [(i) $\Rightarrow$ (iii)] is the same as [(i) $\Rightarrow$ (iv)] of Theorem~\ref{T:Exlocunital}.

For the implication [(iii) $\Rightarrow$ (ii)] we write ${\mathcal{A}}^\#$ for the unconditional unitisation of ${\mathcal{A}}$.
Since ${\mathcal{A}}$ is exact, ${\mathcal{A}}^\#$ is exact and therefore so is ${\mathcal{A}}^\#/{\mathcal{J}}$.
Consider the short exact sequence 
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
0 \arrow[r] & {\mathcal{J}} \arrow[r] & {\mathcal{A}}^\# \arrow[r, "q^\#"] & {\mathcal{A}}^\#/{\mathcal{J}} \arrow[r] & 0
\end{tikzcd}
\]
where $q^\#$ is the natural unital map that extends $q$. 

Let $E\subseteq {\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}}$ be a finite-dimensional selfadjoint subspace, and denote by $\widetilde{E}$ the operator system generated by $E$ inside ${\mathcal{A}}^\#/{\mathcal{J}}$. 
Since ${\mathcal{A}}^\#$ is exact, by Theorem~\ref{T:Exlocunital} we obtain a unital completely positive map $\widetilde{\theta}\colon \widetilde{E} \to {\mathcal{A}}^\#$ such that $q^\#\circ\widetilde{\theta} = {\operatorname{id}}_{\widetilde{E}}$. 
Consider the commutative diagram
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
{\mathcal{A}} \arrow[r] \arrow[d, "q"] & {\mathcal{A}}^\# \arrow[d,"q^\#"] \\
{\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}} \arrow[r] & {\mathcal{A}}^\#/{\mathcal{J}}
\end{tikzcd}
\]
For $x\in E$ we have $\widetilde{\theta}(x) = a + \mu 1_{{\mathcal{A}}^\#}$ where $a\in {\mathcal{A}}$ and $\mu \in \mathbb{C}$. 
Moreover, we have
\[
x = q^\#\circ \widetilde{\theta}(x) = q(a)+\mu 1_{{\mathcal{A}}^\#/{\mathcal{J}}},
\]
which implies that $\mu = 0$ as the unit of ${\mathcal{A}}^\#/{\mathcal{J}}$ is not contained in ${\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}}$ (being the extension by one dimension as a vector space). 
In particular, we get $\widetilde{\theta}(E)\subseteq {\mathcal{A}}$. 
Set 
\[
\theta:= \widetilde{\theta}|_E \colon E \to {\mathcal{A}},
\]
and note that $\theta$ is the required completely contractive and completely positive map satisfying 
\[
q \circ \theta (x) = q^\#|_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \widetilde{\theta}|_E(x) = x \text{ for all } x\in E.
\]

For the implication [(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i)] let $E \subseteq {\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}}$ be a finite-dimensional operator space and apply the hypothesis for the selfadjoint subspace $E'$ generated by $E$ to obtain a completely contractive completely positive map $\theta'\colon E' \to {\mathcal{A}}$ such that $q \circ \theta' = {\operatorname{id}}_{E'}$.
Then the completely contractive restriction map $\theta := \theta'|_E$ is the required local lift.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\iota \colon {\mathcal{A}} \to {\mathcal{J}} + {\mathcal{A}}$ be the canonical embedding and $\pi \colon ({\mathcal{J}}+{\mathcal{A}})/{\mathcal{J}} \to {\mathcal{A}}/({\mathcal{J}}\cap {\mathcal{A}})$ be the canonical $*$-isomorphism. 
We obtain the following commutative diagram
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
0 \arrow[r] & {\mathcal{J}}\cap {\mathcal{A}} \arrow[r] & {\mathcal{A}} \arrow[r, "q_{{\mathcal{A}}}"] \arrow[d, "\iota"] & {\mathcal{A}}/({\mathcal{J}} \cap {\mathcal{A}}) \arrow[r] & 0 \\
0 \arrow[r] & {\mathcal{J}} \arrow[r] & {\mathcal{J}} + {\mathcal{A}} \arrow[r, "q"] & ({\mathcal{J}} + {\mathcal{A}})/{\mathcal{J}} \arrow[r] \arrow[u, "\pi"] & 0
\end{tikzcd}
\]
and since ${\mathcal{A}}$ is exact, we get that ${\mathcal{J}} \cap {\mathcal{A}}$ and ${\mathcal{A}}/({\mathcal{J}} \cap {\mathcal{A}}) \simeq ({\mathcal{J}}+{\mathcal{A}})/{\mathcal{J}}$ are also exact. By Theorem~\ref{T:Exlocgen} we thus obtain that the top short exact sequence is locally split.
By assumption ${\mathcal{J}}$ is also exact, and hence by Theorem~\ref{T:Exlocgen} it suffices to show that the bottom short exact sequence is locally split.

Towards this end, let $E \subseteq ({\mathcal{J}}+{\mathcal{A}})/{\mathcal{J}}$ be a finite-dimensional operator space.
Let $\theta \colon \pi(E) \to {\mathcal{A}}$ be a completely contractive map such that $q_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \theta (\pi(x)) = \pi(x)$ for all $x \in E$.
We then have
\[
q \circ \iota \circ \theta \circ \pi(x) = \pi^{-1} \circ q_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \theta \circ \pi(x) = x \text{ for all } x \in E.
\]
Since $\iota\circ\theta\circ\pi|_E$ is also completely contractive the proof is complete.

label: R:Ex-ext
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{R:Ex-ext}
Let ${\mathcal{A}}$ be an exact C*-algebra and ${\mathcal{J}} \subseteq {\mathcal{A}}$ be an ideal.
Let $E \subseteq {\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}}$ be a finite-dimensional selfadjoint subspace and let $\theta \colon E \to {\mathcal{A}}$ be the completely contractive completely positive local lift of ${\operatorname{id}}_E$ obtained in the proof of Theorem~\ref{T:Exlocgen}.
From the proof of Theorem~\ref{T:Exlocgen} the lift $\theta$ is given as the restriction of a unital completely positive map $\widetilde{\theta}\colon E + \mathbb{C} 1_{{\mathcal{A}}^\#/{\mathcal{J}}} \to {\mathcal{A}}^\#$ for the unconditional unitisation ${\mathcal{A}}^\#$ of ${\mathcal{A}}$.
Suppose we are given a completely contractive and completely positive map 
\[
\alpha \colon {\mathcal{A}} \to M_n(\mathbb{C}).
\]
We want to show that the completely contractive completely positive map 
\[
\alpha \circ \theta \colon E \to M_n(\mathbb{C})
\]
has a completely contractive completely positive extension to the entire ${\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}}$.

Towards this end, we may consider the canonical extension $\alpha^\# \colon {\mathcal{A}}^\# \to M_n(\mathbb{C})$ which is a unital completely positive map, see for example \cite[Lemma 4.9 (c) and Corollary 4.17]{Wer02}.
Then we obtain a unital completely positive map
\[
\alpha^\# \circ \widetilde{\theta} \colon E + \mathbb{C} 1_{{\mathcal{A}}^\#/{\mathcal{J}}} \to M_n(\mathbb{C}),
\]
which by Arveson's Extension Theorem has a unital completely positive extension
\[
\widetilde{\alpha^\# \circ \widetilde{\theta}} \colon {\mathcal{A}}^\#/{\mathcal{J}} \to M_n(\mathbb{C}).
\]
By construction we have that $\widetilde{\alpha^\# \circ \widetilde{\theta}}|_{{\mathcal{A}}/{\mathcal{J}}}$ is a completely contractive completely positive extension of $\alpha \circ \theta$.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let ${\mathcal{A}}$ be a C*-algebra. 
We say that ${\mathcal{A}}$ is \emph{nuclear} if for every C*-algebra ${\mathcal{B}}$ the canonical $*$-epimorphism ${\mathcal{A}}\otimes_{\max} {\mathcal{B}} \to {\mathcal{A}}\otimes {\mathcal{B}}$ is a $*$-isomorphism.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\cite{CE78, Kir77}
Let ${\mathcal{A}}$ be a C*-algebra.
Then ${\mathcal{A}}$ is nuclear if and only if there exist nets of completely contractive completely positive maps $\phi_\lambda \colon {\mathcal{A}} \to M_{k_\lambda}(\mathbb{C})$ and $\psi_\lambda \colon M_{k_\lambda}(\mathbb{C}) \to {\mathcal{A}}$ such that 
\[
\lim_\lambda \| \psi_\lambda \circ \phi_\lambda (a) - a \| = 0 \text{ for all } a\in {\mathcal{A}}.
\]

title: Definition
body_md:
Let ${\mathcal{C}}$ and ${\mathcal{D}}$ be C*-algebras.
A completely contractive completely positive map $\Phi \colon {\mathcal{C}} \to {\mathcal{D}}$ is called \emph{nuclear} if there exist nets of completely contractive completely positive maps $\phi_\lambda \colon {\mathcal{C}} \to M_{k_\lambda}(\mathbb{C})$ and $\psi_\lambda \colon M_{k_\lambda}(\mathbb{C}) \to {\mathcal{D}}$ such that $\lim_\lambda \| \psi_\lambda \circ \phi_\lambda (c) - \Phi(c) \| = 0 \text{ for all } c \in {\mathcal{C}}$.

If ${\mathcal{C}}$ is a C*-subalgebra of ${\mathcal{D}}$ and the inclusion map ${\mathcal{C}} \hookrightarrow {\mathcal{D}}$ is nuclear, then we say that \emph{${\mathcal{C}}$ is nuclearly embedded in ${\mathcal{D}}$}.

label: T:Nucsum
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
To fix notation let
\[
q \colon {\mathcal{J}} + {\mathcal{A}} \to ({\mathcal{J}}+{\mathcal{A}})/{\mathcal{J}}
\quad\text{and}\quad
q_{\mathcal{A}} \colon {\mathcal{A}} \to {\mathcal{A}}/({\mathcal{J}} \cap {\mathcal{A}})
\]
be the canonical quotient maps, and consider the $*$-isomorphism
\[
\pi \colon ({\mathcal{J}}+{\mathcal{A}})/{\mathcal{J}} \to {\mathcal{A}}/({\mathcal{J}}\cap{\mathcal{A}}),
\]
that satisfies $\pi \circ q|_{\mathcal{A}} = q_{\mathcal{A}}$.
Henceforth, fix a finite set ${\mathcal{F}} \subseteq {\mathcal{J}}+{\mathcal{A}}$ of contractions and $\varepsilon>0$, and consider the finite-dimensional selfadjoint subspace
\[
E := \operatorname{span}\{ \pi \circ q (x), \pi \circ q(x)^* \mid x \in {\mathcal{F}} \} \subseteq {\mathcal{A}}/({\mathcal{J}}\cap{\mathcal{A}}).
\]
Since ${\mathcal{A}}$ is nuclearly embedded in ${\mathcal{C}}$ it is also exact, and hence so are ${\mathcal{J}} \cap {\mathcal{A}}$ and ${\mathcal{A}}/({\mathcal{J}} \cap {\mathcal{A}})$.
Therefore Theorem~\ref{T:Exlocgen} applies to the short exact sequence
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}
0 \arrow[r] & {\mathcal{J}} \cap {\mathcal{A}} \arrow[r] & {\mathcal{A}} \arrow[r,"q_{{\mathcal{A}}}"] & {\mathcal{A}}/({\mathcal{J}} \cap {\mathcal{A}}) \arrow[r] & 0
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}
and yields a completely contractive completely positive map $\theta \colon E \to {\mathcal{A}}$ such that $q_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \theta = {\operatorname{id}}_E$.
Since $\theta(\pi \circ q(x)) \in {\mathcal{A}}$ we get
\[
\pi \circ q \circ \theta(\pi \circ q(x)) = q_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \theta(\pi \circ q(x)) = \pi \circ q(x),
\]
and since $\pi$ is a $*$-isomorphism we get
\[
q \circ \theta(\pi \circ q(x)) = q(x).
\]
Hence we obtain
\[
b_x := \theta(\pi \circ q(x)) - x \in {\mathcal{J}} \text{ for all } x \in {\mathcal{F}}.
\]

Since ${\mathcal{A}}$ is nuclearly embedded in ${\mathcal{C}}$, for the finite set of contractions $\{ \theta(\pi \circ q(x)) \mid x \in {\mathcal{F}}\}$ and for the fixed $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and completely contractive completely positive maps $\alpha_{\mathcal{A}} \colon {\mathcal{A}} \to M_n(\mathbb{C})$ and $\beta_{\mathcal{A}} \colon M_n(\mathbb{C}) \to {\mathcal{C}}$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{Eq:nucquot}
\| \beta_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \alpha_{\mathcal{A}} (\theta(\pi \circ q(x))) - \theta(\pi \circ q(x)) \| < \varepsilon \text{ for all } x \in {\mathcal{F}}.
\end{equation}
By Remark~\ref{R:Ex-ext} there exists a completely contractive completely positive map 
\[
\widetilde{\alpha_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \theta} \colon {\mathcal{A}}/({\mathcal{J}} \cap {\mathcal{A}}) \to M_n(\mathbb{C}) \text{ such that } \widetilde{\alpha_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \theta}|_E = \alpha_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \theta.
\]
By setting
\[
\widehat{\alpha}_{\mathcal{A}} := \widetilde{\alpha_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \theta} \circ \pi \circ q \colon {\mathcal{J}} + {\mathcal{A}} \to M_n(\mathbb{C}),
\]
we obtain a completely contractive completely positive map with
\[
\widehat{\alpha}_{\mathcal{A}}(x) = \widetilde{\alpha_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \theta}(\pi \circ q (x)) = \alpha_{\mathcal{A}}(\theta(\pi \circ q(x)))
\text{ for all } x \in {\mathcal{F}}.
\]
Using \eqref{Eq:nucquot} we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{Eq:nucGa}
\| \beta_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \widehat{\alpha}_{\mathcal{A}} (x) - x - b_x \| = \| \beta_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \alpha_{\mathcal{A}}(\theta(\pi \circ q(x))) - \theta(\pi \circ q(x)) \| < \varepsilon \text{ for all } x \in {\mathcal{F}}.
\end{equation}

We next use the canonical embeddings
\[
{\mathcal{J}}^\# \subseteq ({\mathcal{J}} + {\mathcal{A}})^\# \subseteq {\mathcal{C}}^\#
\]
for the unconditional unitisations.
Fix continuous functions $u, v \colon [0,1] \to [0,1]$ such that
\[
u(s) = 0 \quad\text{for}\quad s \leq 1/2,
\quad
u(1) = 1,
\quad
v(s) = 0 \quad\text{for}\quad s \leq 1/4,
\quad
v(s) = 1 \quad\text{for}\quad s \geq 1/2,
\]
and set $k := (1 - u^2)^{1/2}$.
By construction we have
\begin{equation}\label{Eq:nucfun}
u^2 + k^2 = 1,
\quad
u v = u,
\quad
u(0) = v(0) = 0
\quad\text{and}\quad
k(1) = 0.
\end{equation}
By \cite[Theorem 3.12.14]{Ped79} we may pick an approximate unit $(e_\lambda)_\lambda$ of ${\mathcal{J}}$ consisting of positive contractions which is quasicentral in ${\mathcal{J}}+{\mathcal{A}}$, that is
\[
\lim_\lambda \| e_\lambda y - y e_\lambda \| = 0 \text{ for all } y \in {\mathcal{J}} + {\mathcal{A}}.
\]

We will use two standard consequences of the continuous functional calculus, which we perform in $({\mathcal{J}}+{\mathcal{A}})^\#$.
Note that since each $e_\lambda$ is a positive contraction we have $\sigma(e_\lambda) \subseteq [0,1]$, and therefore
\begin{equation}\label{Eq:nucfc}
\| f(e_\lambda) \| \leq \|f\|_\infty := \sup\{ |f(s)| \mid s \in [0,1] \} \text{ for all } f \in C[0,1].
\end{equation}
 
 Firstly, quasicentrality passes to the continuous functional calculus, in the sense that
\begin{equation}\label{Eq:nucqc}
\lim_\lambda \| f(e_\lambda) y - y f(e_\lambda) \| = 0 \text{ for all } y \in {\mathcal{J}}+{\mathcal{A}} \text{ and } f \in C[0,1].
\end{equation}
Indeed, for $j \geq 1$ the telescoping identity
\[
e_\lambda^j y - y e_\lambda^j = \sum_{i=0}^{j-1} e_\lambda^i \, ( e_\lambda y - y e_\lambda ) \, e_\lambda^{j-1-i}
\]
together with $\|e_\lambda\| \leq 1$ gives 
\[
\|e_\lambda^j y - y e_\lambda^j\| \leq j \|e_\lambda y - y e_\lambda\|.
\]
As scalar multiples of the unit are central, for every polynomial $p(s) = \sum_{j=0}^N c_j s^j$ we obtain
\[
\| p(e_\lambda) y - y p(e_\lambda) \| \leq \Big( \sum_{j=1}^N j |c_j| \Big) \| e_\lambda y - y e_\lambda \| \xrightarrow{\ \lambda \ } 0.
\]
Now let $f \in C[0,1]$ and $\varepsilon'>0$, and use the Stone--Weierstrass Theorem to pick a polynomial $p$ with $\|f - p\|_\infty < \varepsilon'$, so that $\|f(e_\lambda) - p(e_\lambda)\| < \varepsilon'$ for all $\lambda$ by \eqref{Eq:nucfc}.
Then
\[
\limsup_\lambda \| f(e_\lambda) y - y f(e_\lambda) \|
\leq
2 \varepsilon' \|y\| + \limsup_\lambda \| p(e_\lambda) y - y p(e_\lambda) \|
=
2 \varepsilon' \|y\|,
\]
and letting $\varepsilon' \to 0$ establishes \eqref{Eq:nucqc}.
 
Secondly, since $(e_\lambda)_\lambda$ is an approximate unit for ${\mathcal{J}}$ we have
\begin{equation}\label{Eq:nucau}
\lim_\lambda \| f(e_\lambda) d - f(1) d \| = 0 \text{ for all } d \in {\mathcal{J}} \text{ and } f \in C[0,1].
\end{equation}
Indeed, for $f(s) = s^j$ with $j \geq 1$ this follows by induction on $j$ from the identity
\[
e_\lambda^j d - d = e_\lambda^{j-1} ( e_\lambda d - d ) + ( e_\lambda^{j-1} d - d )
\]
and $\|e_\lambda\| \leq 1$, and it also holds trivially for $j=0$.
By linearity it holds for $f$ being a polynomial.
For arbitrary $f \in C[0,1]$ and $\varepsilon' > 0$ pick a polynomial $p$ with $\|f - p\|_\infty < \varepsilon'$.
Then we get $|f(1) - p(1)| < \varepsilon'$, and we also have
\[
\| f(e_\lambda) d - f(1) d \|
\leq
\| f(e_\lambda) - p(e_\lambda) \| \, \|d\| + \| p(e_\lambda) d - p(1) d \| + | p(1) - f(1) | \, \|d\|.
\]
Therefore by using \eqref{Eq:nucfc} we get
\[
\limsup_\lambda \| f(e_\lambda) d - f(1) d \| \leq 2 \varepsilon' \|d\|,
\]
and \eqref{Eq:nucau} follows.
Applying \eqref{Eq:nucau} to $f = k$ and using $k(1) = 0$ from \eqref{Eq:nucfun} we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{Eq:nuck}
\lim_\lambda \| k(e_\lambda) d \| = 0 \text{ for all } d \in {\mathcal{J}}.
\end{equation}
 
Using \eqref{Eq:nucqc} and \eqref{Eq:nuck} we may fix $\lambda$ such that the positive contractions
\[
U := u(e_\lambda) \in {\mathcal{J}},
\quad
V := v(e_\lambda) \in {\mathcal{J}}
\quad\text{and}\quad
K := k(e_\lambda) \in ({\mathcal{J}}+{\mathcal{A}})^\#
\]
satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{Eq:nucpart}
\| x - U x U - K x K \| < \varepsilon
\quad\text{and}\quad
\| K b_x K \| < \varepsilon
\text{ for all } x \in {\mathcal{F}}.
\end{equation}
Indeed, the fact that $U, V \in {\mathcal{J}}$ follows by noting that $u(0)=v(0)=0$ (and hence $u$, $v$ can be taken as limits of polynomials with zero constant term) and $e_\lambda \in {\mathcal{J}}$. 
The first estimate follows by using the equality
\[
U x U + K x K = U^2 x + K^2 x + U[x,U] + K[x,K] = x + U[x,U]+K[x,K],
\]
which is obtained by \eqref{Eq:nucfun}, and noting that both commutators vanish in the limit by \eqref{Eq:nucqc}. 
The second estimate follows from \eqref{Eq:nuck} and the fact that $b_x\in {\mathcal{J}}$.

Since ${\mathcal{J}}$ is an ideal of ${\mathcal{J}} + {\mathcal{A}}$ we have $V y V \in {\mathcal{J}}$ for every $y \in {\mathcal{J}} + {\mathcal{A}}$. 
In particular, we have that the finite set $\{V x V \mid x\in {\mathcal{F}}\}$ sits inside ${\mathcal{J}}$.
Using that ${\mathcal{J}}$ is nuclearly embedded in ${\mathcal{C}}$, we may pick $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and completely contractive completely positive maps $\alpha_{\mathcal{J}} \colon {\mathcal{J}} \to M_m(\mathbb{C})$ and $\beta_{\mathcal{J}} \colon M_m(\mathbb{C}) \to {\mathcal{C}}$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{Eq:nucid}
\| \beta_{\mathcal{J}} \circ \alpha_{\mathcal{J}} (V x V) - V x V \| < \varepsilon \text{ for all } x \in {\mathcal{F}}.
\end{equation}

To complete the proof, consider the maps
\begin{align*}
\Phi & \colon {\mathcal{J}} + {\mathcal{A}} \to M_m(\mathbb{C}) \oplus M_n(\mathbb{C});\
\Phi(y) = \alpha_{\mathcal{J}}(V y V) \oplus \widehat{\alpha}_{\mathcal{A}}(y),
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
\Psi & \colon M_m(\mathbb{C}) \oplus M_n(\mathbb{C}) \to {\mathcal{C}};\
\Psi(y_1 \oplus y_2) = U \beta_{\mathcal{J}}(y_1) U + K \beta_{\mathcal{A}}(y_2) K.
\end{align*}
The map $\Psi$ indeed takes values in ${\mathcal{C}}$ as ${\mathcal{C}}$ is an ideal of ${\mathcal{C}}^\#$.
The map $\Phi$ is completely positive and completely contractive as a direct sum of such maps.
The map $\Psi$ is completely positive, and since $\beta_{\mathcal{J}}$ and $\beta_{\mathcal{A}}$ are contractive we have $\beta_{\mathcal{J}}(1) \leq 1$ and $\beta_{\mathcal{A}}(1) \leq 1$ in ${\mathcal{C}}^\#$, whence
\[
\Psi(1 \oplus 1) = U \beta_{\mathcal{J}}(1) U + K \beta_{\mathcal{A}}(1) K \leq U^2 + K^2 = 1.
\]
As completely positive maps on unital C*-algebras attain their cb-norm at the unit, we conclude that $\Psi$ is completely contractive.

It remains to estimate $\Psi \circ \Phi$ on ${\mathcal{F}}$.
Since $UV = VU = U$ by \eqref{Eq:nucfun}, equation \eqref{Eq:nucid} gives
\[
\| U \beta_{\mathcal{J}} \circ \alpha_{\mathcal{J}} (V x V) U - U x U \|
=
\| U \big( \beta_{\mathcal{J}} \circ \alpha_{\mathcal{J}} (VxV) - VxV \big) U \|
< \varepsilon,
\]
while \eqref{Eq:nucGa} and the second estimate of \eqref{Eq:nucpart} give
\[
\| K \beta_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \widehat{\alpha}_{\mathcal{A}}(x) K - K x K \|
\leq
\| K \big( \beta_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \widehat{\alpha}_{\mathcal{A}} (x) - x - b_x \big) K \| + \| K b_x K \|
<
2 \varepsilon.
\]
Combining with the first estimate of \eqref{Eq:nucpart}, for every $x\in {\mathcal{F}}$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
\| \Psi \circ \Phi(x) - x \|
& =
\| U \beta_{\mathcal{J}} \circ \alpha_{\mathcal{J}} (V x V) U + K \beta_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \widehat{\alpha}_{\mathcal{A}}(x) K - x \| \\
& \leq
\| U \beta_{\mathcal{J}} \circ \alpha_{\mathcal{J}} (V x V) U - U x U \|
+ \| K \beta_{\mathcal{A}} \circ \widehat{\alpha}_{\mathcal{A}}(x) K - K x K \| + \\
& \hspace{5.34cm} + \| U x U + K x K - x \| \\
& <
\varepsilon + 2 \varepsilon + \varepsilon
=
4 \varepsilon.
\end{align*}
Since ${\mathcal{F}}$ and $\varepsilon$ were arbitrary, the inclusion of ${\mathcal{J}} + {\mathcal{A}}$ in ${\mathcal{C}}$ is nuclear and the proof is complete.

label: R:ideal
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{R:ideal}
For a finite $\cap$-closed ${\mathcal{F}} \subseteq {\mathcal{J}}$ we set 
\[
\mathbf{B}_{{\mathcal{F}}, t_\ast} := \sum_{{\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{F}}} \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, t_\ast},
\]
which is again a C*-subalgebra of $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$.
Indeed, let ${\mathcal{F}} \subseteq {\mathcal{J}}$ be finite and $\cap$-closed.
Since ${\mathcal{F}}$ is finite we may pick ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{F}}$ to be maximal in ${\mathcal{F}}$ with respect to inclusion.
Maximality of ${\mathbf{x}}$ implies that ${\mathcal{F}}' := {\mathcal{F}} \setminus \{{\mathbf{x}}\}$ is also $\cap$-closed and that ${\mathbf{x}} \cap {\mathbf{y}} \in {\mathcal{F}}'$ for every ${\mathbf{y}} \in {\mathcal{F}}'$.
Using $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},t_\ast} \cdot \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{y}},t_\ast}\subseteq \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}\cap {\mathbf{y}},t_\ast}$ we get that $\mathbf{B}_{{\mathcal{F}}', t_\ast}$ is an ideal in $\mathbf{B}_{{\mathcal{F}},t_\ast}$.
Hence an induction over the size of ${\mathcal{F}}$ gives that $\mathbf{B}_{{\mathcal{F}}, t_\ast}$ is closed as the sum of an ideal and a C*-subalgebra.

If $t$ is equivariant, then the fixed point algebra $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$ is the inductive limit of the $\mathbf{B}_{{\mathcal{F}}, t_\ast}$ over the finite $\cap$-closed $\emptyset\in {\mathcal{F}} \subseteq {\mathcal{J}}$.

body_md:
\label{P:fanoeps}
Let $P$ be a unital subsemigroup of a discrete group $G$ and let $X$ be a non-degenerate product system over $P$.
Let $t$ be a representation of $X$.
Then for every ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$ the core $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, t_\ast}$ is the closed linear span of the spaces
\[
t_{p_1}(X_{p_1})^* t_{q_1}(X_{q_1}) \cdots
t_{p_n}(X_{p_n})^* t_{q_n}(X_{q_n})
\]
over all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $p_1, q_1, \dots, p_n, q_n \in P$ with
$p_1^{-1} q_1 \cdots p_n^{-1} q_n = e_P$ and
$q_n^{-1} p_n \dots q_1^{-1} p_1 P = {\mathbf{x}}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Non-degeneracy gives $[A \cdot X_q] = X_q$, and hence $A \cdot X_q = X_q$ by the Cohen Factorisation Theorem.
Let $\xi_q \in X_q$ and write $\xi_q = a \xi_q'$ with $a \in A$ and $\xi_q' \in X_q$.
Then
\[
t_{e_P}(a^*)^* t_q(\xi_q') = t_q(a \xi_q') = t_q(\xi_q)
\quad\text{and}\quad
t_q(\xi_q)^* = t_q(\xi_q')^* t_{e_P}(a^*).
\]
Applying the first identity to the leftmost factor of a word with $\varepsilon = 0$ produces a word with $\varepsilon = 1$ and $p_1 = e_P$, and applying the second to the rightmost factor of a word with $\varepsilon' = 0$ produces a word with $\varepsilon' = 1$ and $q_n = e_P$.
Neither operation changes the group element $p_1^{-\varepsilon} q_1 \cdots p_n^{-1} q_n^{\varepsilon'}$ nor the constructible ideal $q_n^{-\varepsilon'} p_n \dots q_1^{-1} p_1^{\varepsilon} P$, as $e_P$ acts trivially in both expressions.

label: R:scr
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{R:scr}
Let $P$ be a unital subsemigroup of a discrete group $G$ and let $X$ be a product system over $P$. 
We write $A\times_X P$ for the universal boundary quotient of ${\mathcal{T}}(X)$ constructed by Sehnem in \cite[Theorem~3.10]{Seh19}. 
Every strong covariant representation of $X$ in the sense of \cite[Definition~3.2]{Seh19} is Fock covariant, since the strong covariance relations are graded and are induced from ${\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)$, see \cite[Section~5]{DKKLL22}. 
In \cite[Lemma~3.4]{Seh19} it is shown that $A\times_X P$ is an equivariant quotient of ${\mathcal{T}}(X)$, i.e., it inherits a coaction by $G$.
As observed in \cite[Section~5]{DKKLL22} this gives rise to a Fell bundle ${\mathcal{S}}{\mathcal{C}} X$ over $G$, and $A\times_X P$ is the full cross-sectional C*-algebra of ${\mathcal{S}}{\mathcal{C}} X$. 
We write $A\times_{X,\lambda} P$ for the corresponding reduced cross-sectional C*-algebra, which inherits a normal coaction by $G$. 
Since $A\times_{X,\lambda} P$ is a quotient of $A\times_X P$, every $*$-representation of either algebra arises from a Fock covariant representation of $X$. Consequently, all results we obtain for Fock covariant representations also apply to the boundary quotients $A\times_X P$ and $A\times_{X,\lambda} P$.

label: E:semig
title: Example
body_md:
\label{E:semig}
Let $P$ be a unital subsemigroup of a discrete group $G$.
A map $w\colon P \to {\mathcal{B}}(H)$ is called an \emph{isometric representation of $P$} if it is a semigroup homomorphism and each $w_p$ is an isometry.
Following the notation of \cite{LS22}, for a word of even length we write $\alpha = (p_1, q_1, \dots, p_n, q_n)$ where $p_1, q_1, \dots, p_n, q_n\in P$.
A word $\alpha = (p_1, q_1, \dots, p_n, q_n)$ is called \emph{neutral} if $p_1^{-1} q_1 \cdots p_n^{-1} q_n = e_P$.
We also write
\[
K(\alpha) := q_n^{-1} p_n \dots q_1^{-1} p_1 P
\]
for the induced constructible ideal in ${\mathcal{J}}$, and
\[
\dot{w}_\alpha := w_{p_1}^* w_{q_1} \cdots w_{p_n}^* w_{q_n} \in {\mathcal{B}}(H).
\]

Let ${\mathcal{T}}(P):=\mathrm{C}^*(\{v_p \mid p\in P\})$ denote the universal C*-algebra with respect to isometric representations of $P$.
Moreover, we write $\mathrm{C}^*_\lambda(P)$ for the reduced C*-algebra of the semigroup which is generated by the left regular representation $V\colon P \to {\mathcal{B}}(\ell^2(P))$.
In \cite{LS22} the exact algebraic relations that describe Fock covariance are identified.
Following the notation of \cite{LS22} we denote by ${\mathcal{T}}_u(P)$ the universal C*-algebra with respect to (isometric) representations $w \colon P \to {\mathcal{B}}(H)$ that satisfy the relations:
\begin{itemize}
\item [\rm{(T1)}] $w_{e_P}=1$;
\item [\rm{(T2)}] $\dot{w}_{\alpha}=0$ if $K(\alpha)=\emptyset$ for a neutral word $\alpha$;
\item [\rm{(T3)}] $\dot{w}_{\alpha}=\dot{w}_{\beta}$ if $K(\alpha)=K(\beta)$ for neutral words $\alpha$ and $\beta$; and
\item [\rm{(T4)}] $\prod_{\beta\in F}(\dot{w}_{\alpha}-\dot{w}_{\beta})=0$ whenever $\alpha$ is a neutral word, $F$ is a finite set of neutral words and $K(\alpha)=\bigcup_{\beta\in F}K(\beta)$.
\end{itemize}
These relations are of course satisfied by the left regular representation $V$ of $P$.

We define the concrete product system $X_P$ in ${\mathcal{T}}(P)$ by
\[
X_{P, p} := \mathbb{C} v_p \text{ for all } p \in P.
\]
Then the association
\[
t = \{t_p\}_{p \in P} \mapsto w_t = \{t_p(v_p)\}_{p \in P}
\]
defines a bijection between unital (Fock covariant) representations of $X_P$ and isometric representations of $P$ (resp.\ that satisfy conditions (T1)--(T4)).
This bijection matches the Fock representation $\lambda$ of $X_P$ to the left regular representation $V$ of $P$.
See \cite[Proposition 3.9]{KP25} for a detailed proof.
In particular, we obtain the canonical $*$-isomorphisms
\[
{\mathcal{T}}(X_P)\simeq {\mathcal{T}}(P), \quad {\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X_P)\simeq \mathrm{C}^*_\lambda(P) \quad\text{and}\quad{\mathcal{T}}_{\operatorname{c}}^{\operatorname{F}}(X_P)\simeq {\mathcal{T}}_u(P).
\]
Hence, if $G$ is assumed amenable, then we get $\mathrm{C}^*_\lambda(P) \simeq {\mathcal{T}}_u(P)$.

Moreover, let $w$ be an isometric representation of $P$ that satisfies conditions (T1)--(T4) and let $t$ be its corresponding Fock covariant representation of $X_P$.
Let ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$ be a constructible ideal.
If ${\mathbf{x}}=\emptyset$, then condition (T2) implies that $\mathbf{K}_{\emptyset,t_\ast}=(0)$.
If ${\mathbf{x}}\neq \emptyset$, then pick a neutral word $\alpha=(p_1,q_1,\dots,p_n,q_n)$ such that ${\mathbf{x}} = K(\alpha)$.
In this case, condition (T3) implies that 
\[
\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},t_\ast} = \mathbb{C} \dot{w}_\alpha.
\]

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) If $z=e_P$, then the result follows trivially.
Suppose that $z\neq e_P$.
We have 
\[
X_z \otimes_A X_{z^{-1}} \simeq X_{e_P} = A,
\]
so it suffices to show this for the elements $a := u_{z, z^{-1}}(\xi_z \otimes \eta_{z^{-1}})$ with $\xi_z \in X_z$ and $\eta_{z^{-1}} \in X_{z^{-1}}$.
For $\zeta_z \in X_z$ we have $\eta_{z^{-1}} \otimes \zeta_z \in X_{z^{-1}} \otimes_A X_z \simeq A$, and therefore
\begin{align*}
\varphi_{z}(a) \zeta_z
& =
u_{e_P,z} \circ (u_{z,z^{-1}} \otimes {\operatorname{id}}_{X_{z}})((\xi_z \otimes \eta_{z^{-1}}) \otimes \zeta_z) \\
& =
u_{z, e_P} \circ ({\operatorname{id}}_{X_z} \otimes u_{z^{-1},z})(\xi_z \otimes (\eta_{z^{-1}} \otimes \zeta_z)) \\
& =
M^{e_P, z}_{\xi_z} \left( M^{z, e_P}_{\eta_{z^{-1}}} \zeta_z \right).
\end{align*}
Thus $\varphi_{z}(a) = M^{e_P,z}_{\xi_z} \circ M^{z, e_P}_{\eta_{z^{-1}}}$, which lies in ${\mathcal{K}}(X_z)$ since $M^{e_P,z}_{\xi_z} \in {\mathcal{K}}(A, X_z)$ by Lemma~\ref{L:famult} and $M^{z,e_P}_{\eta_{z^{-1}}} \in {\mathcal{L}}(X_z, A)$.
The claim follows by linearity and continuity.

\smallskip
\noindent
(ii) It suffices to consider $S = \theta^{X_q, X_p}_{\xi_p, \eta_q}$ with $\xi_p \in X_p$ and $\eta_q \in X_q$.
Since $[X_q \cdot A] = X_q$, the Cohen Factorisation Theorem allows us to write $\eta_q = \eta'_q a$ with $\eta'_q \in X_q$ and $a \in A$.
For $\zeta_q \in X_q$ and $\kappa_z \in X_z$ we then have
\begin{align*}
i^z_{p,q}(S) \left( u_{q,z}(\zeta_q \otimes \kappa_z) \right)
&=
u_{p,z} \left( \xi_p \left\langle\eta_q, \zeta_q\right\rangle \otimes \kappa_z \right)\\
&=
u_{p,z} \left( \xi_p \otimes
\varphi_{z}(a^*) \varphi_{z}(\left\langle\eta'_q, \zeta_q\right\rangle) \kappa_z \right)\\
&=
i^z_{p, e_P} \left( M^{e_P,p}_{\xi_p} \right) \;
\varphi_{z}(a^*) \;
i^z_{e_P, q} \left( \left( M^{e_P,q}_{\eta'_q} \right)^* \right)\left( u_{q,z}(\zeta_q \otimes \kappa_z) \right),
\end{align*}
and hence
\[
i^z_{p,q}(S)
=
i^z_{p, e_P} \left( M^{e_P,p}_{\xi_p} \right) \;
\varphi_{z}(a^*) \;
i^z_{e_P, q} \left( \left( M^{e_P,q}_{\eta'_q} \right)^* \right).
\]
The outer two factors are adjointable and the middle one is compact by item (i), and thus $i^z_{p,q}(S) \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_{qz}, X_{pz})$. By linearity and continuity the proof is complete.

title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{C:Excores-3}
Let $P$ be a unital subsemigroup of an exact discrete group $G$ and let $X$ be a product system over $P$.
Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item ${\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)$ is exact.
\item $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast}$ is exact for every ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$.
\item $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$ is exact for a quotient $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$ of ${\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)$ that is injective on $A$.
\item $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},t_\ast}$ is exact for every ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$, for a quotient $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$ of ${\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)$ that is injective on $A$.
\item $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$ is exact for an injective equivariant Fock covariant representation $t$ of $X$ that admits a normal coaction.
\item $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},t_\ast}$ is exact for every ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$, for an injective equivariant Fock covariant representation $t$ of $X$ that admits a normal coaction.
\end{enumerate}
If any of the items above holds, then items (iii)--(vi) hold for any representation $t$ with the properties of the corresponding item.

[(i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii)].
Each $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, \lambda_\ast}$ is a C*-subalgebra of ${\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)$ and exactness passes to C*-subalgebras.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i)].
The Fock representation is equivariant, and thus the fixed point algebra $[{\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)]_{e_P}$ is the inductive limit of the $\mathbf{B}_{{\mathcal{F}}, \lambda_\ast}$ over the finite $\cap$-closed $\emptyset \in {\mathcal{F}} \subseteq {\mathcal{J}}$.
Hence Theorem~\ref{T:Kcores} yields that $[{\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)]_{e_P}$ is exact.
Exactness of the group and \cite[Proposition 25.12]{Exe17} (which applies due to normality of the coaction on ${\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)$) then give that ${\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)$ is exact.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(ii) $\Leftrightarrow$ (iv)].
This follows from Proposition~\ref{P:Kcoresiso} due to injectivity of $t$.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(ii) $\Leftrightarrow$ (vi)].
Same as [(ii) $\Leftrightarrow$ (iv)].

\smallskip
\noindent
[(i) $\Rightarrow$ (iii)].
This is immediate as exactness is preserved under quotients.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(iii) $\Rightarrow$ (iv)].
Every $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, t_\ast}$ is a C*-subalgebra of $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$ and exactness passes to C*-subalgebras.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(i) $\Rightarrow$ (v)].
If $t$ is an equivariant Fock covariant representation of $X$ that admits a normal coaction, then $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$ is a quotient of ${\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)$, see for example \cite[comments prior to Proposition~2.1]{KP25}.
Hence this follows as exactness is preserved under quotients.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(v) $\Rightarrow$ (vi)].
Same as [(iii) $\Rightarrow$ (iv)].

label: T:Nuccores
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\noindent
[(i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii)].
Let ${\mathcal{F}} \subseteq {\mathcal{J}}$ be finite and $\cap$-closed.
We show that $\mathbf{B}_{{\mathcal{F}},t_\ast}$ is nuclearly embedded in $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$ by induction on $|{\mathcal{F}}|$.
If $|{\mathcal{F}}| = 1$, then $\mathbf{B}_{{\mathcal{F}},t_\ast} = \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},t_\ast}$ for some ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{F}}$, and the claim holds by hypothesis.
Now suppose that $|{\mathcal{F}}| = k+1$ and that the claim holds for all finite and $\cap$-closed families of cardinality at most $k$.
Write ${\mathcal{F}}'={\mathcal{F}} \setminus \{{\mathbf{x}}\}$ with ${\mathbf{x}}$ maximal in ${\mathcal{F}}$, so that ${\mathcal{F}}'$ is $\cap$-closed and, by Remark~\ref{R:ideal}, the C*-algebra $\mathbf{B}_{{\mathcal{F}}',t_\ast}$ is an ideal in $\mathbf{B}_{{\mathcal{F}},t_\ast} = \mathbf{B}_{{\mathcal{F}}',t_\ast} + \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},t_\ast}$.
By the inductive hypothesis $\mathbf{B}_{{\mathcal{F}}',t_\ast}$ is nuclearly embedded in $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$, and by our hypothesis so is $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},t_\ast}$.
An application of Theorem~\ref{T:Nucsum}
yields that $\mathbf{B}_{{\mathcal{F}},t_\ast}$ is nuclearly embedded in $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$, completing the induction.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i)].
This is immediate by applying item (ii) to ${\mathcal{F}} = \{{\mathbf{x}}\}$.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (iii)].
The fixed point algebra $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$ is the inductive limit of the C*-subalgebras $\mathbf{B}_{{\mathcal{F}},t_\ast}$ over the $\cap$-closed and finite $\emptyset \in {\mathcal{F}} \subseteq {\mathcal{J}}$.
Since the inclusions $\mathbf{B}_{{\mathcal{F}},t_\ast} \hookrightarrow [\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$ are nuclear we obtain that $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$ is nuclear.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(iii) $\Rightarrow$ (ii)].
This is immediate.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(iii) $\Rightarrow$ (iv)].
By \cite[Theorem 20.7 and Proposition 20.2]{Exe17} amenability of $G$ gives
\[
\mathrm{C}^*(t) \simeq \mathrm{C}^*_\lambda(\{[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_g\}_g) \simeq \mathrm{C}^*_{\max}(\{[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_g\}_g),
\]
and the nuclear C*-algebra $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$ is the unit fibre of this Fell bundle.
Hence $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$ is nuclear by \cite[Proposition~25.10]{Exe17}.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(iv) $\Rightarrow$ (iii)].
Let $\delta$ be the coaction by $G$ on $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$ and let ${\mathcal{E}}_\delta\colon \mathrm{C}^*(t) \to [\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$ be the induced conditional expectation.
If $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$ is nuclear, then the inclusion $\iota \colon [\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P} \to \mathrm{C}^*(t)$ is nuclear, and therefore so is ${\operatorname{id}}_{[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}} = {\mathcal{E}}_\delta \circ \iota$,
showing that $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$ is nuclear.

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Example~\ref{E:semig} we have $\mathrm{C}^*_\lambda(P)\simeq {\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X_P)$ and that $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, \lambda_\ast}$ is a finite-dimensional C*-algebra for every ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$, and hence nuclear.
Theorem~\ref{T:Nuccores} then yields that ${\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X_P)$ is nuclear.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Unlike Corollary~\ref{C:exsem}, we recall that Corollary~\ref{C:nucsem} does not hold if $G$ is just assumed exact.
For an example, let $G = P = \mathbb{F}_2$ and consider the product system $X$ over $P$ with $X_p = \mathbb{C}$ for all $p \in P$.
Every non-empty constructible ideal of a group equals the group itself, so that ${\mathcal{J}} = \{\emptyset, P\}$, and the Fock representation gives
\[
{\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X) = \mathrm{C}^*_\lambda(\mathbb{F}_2),
\quad
\mathbf{K}_{\emptyset,\lambda_\ast}=(0) \quad\text{and}\quad
\mathbf{K}_{P, \lambda_\ast} = [{\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)]_{e_P} = \mathbb{C}.
\]
While the $\mathbf{K}$-cores are nuclear, $\mathrm{C}^*_\lambda(\mathbb{F}_2)$ is not nuclear.
We note that $\mathrm{C}^*_\lambda(\mathbb{F}_2)$ is exact, so this example is consistent with Corollary~\ref{C:Excores-3}.

Moreover the converse of Corollary~\ref{C:nucsem} does not hold, i.e., it may be that $\mathrm{C}^*_\lambda(P)$ is nuclear but $P$ cannot be embedded in any amenable group.
A counterexample was provided recently by Dor-On--Li \cite{DL26}.

label: L:famax
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{L:famax}
Let $P$ be a unital subsemigroup of a discrete group $G$.
Let ${\mathbf{x}}$ be a right ideal of $P$ and let $\{p_1, \dots, p_m\}$ be an irredundant generating family for ${\mathbf{x}}$.
If $q \in {\mathbf{x}}$ satisfies $p_i \in q P$ for some $i$, then $q P = p_i P$ and $p_i = q x$ for a unique $x \in P^*$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $q \in {\mathbf{x}}$ we have $q \in p_j P$ for some $j$, and therefore $p_i P \subseteq q P \subseteq p_j P$.
Irredundancy forces $j = i$, and thus $q P = p_i P$.
Write $p_i = q x$ and $q = p_i y$ with $x, y \in P$.
Then 
\[
p_i e_P = p_i = p_i (y x),
\]
and left cancellation gives $y x = e_P$.
Since this identity takes place in $G$ we get $x^{-1} = y \in P$, and hence $x \in P^*$.
Uniqueness follows from left cancellation.
head: environment

label: L:fairr
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{L:fairr}
Let $P$ be a unital subsemigroup of a discrete group $G$.
Let ${\mathbf{x}}$ be a right ideal of $P$ admitting a finite generating family, and let 
\[
\{s_1, \dots, s_m\} \text{ and } \{q_1, \dots, q_k\}
\]
be irredundant generating families for ${\mathbf{x}}$.
Then $m = k$ and there is a bijection $\sigma$ of $\{1, \dots, m\}$ and elements $x_i \in P^*$ such that $s_i = q_{\sigma(i)} x_i$ for all $i$.
Consequently, ${\mathbf{x}}$ is a disjoint union of finitely many principal right ideals if and only if $s_i P \cap s_j P = \emptyset$ for all $i \neq j$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $s_i \in {\mathbf{x}} = \bigcup_j q_j P$ we may pick $\sigma(i)$ with $s_i \in q_{\sigma(i)} P$, and likewise we may pick $\tau(j)$ with $q_j \in s_{\tau(j)} P$.
Then
\[
s_i P \subseteq q_{\sigma(i)} P \subseteq s_{\tau \sigma (i)} P,
\]
and irredundancy of $\{s_1, \dots, s_m\}$ forces $\tau \sigma (i) = i$;
symmetrically $\sigma \tau (j) = j$.
Hence $\sigma$ and $\tau$ are mutually inverse bijections and $m = k$.
Moreover $s_i P = q_{\sigma(i)} P$, and Lemma~\ref{L:famax} applied to $q := q_{\sigma(i)} \in {\mathbf{x}}$ and the irredundant family $\{s_1, \dots, s_m\}$ gives $s_i = q_{\sigma(i)} x_i$ with $x_i \in P^*$.

For the last statement, suppose ${\mathbf{x}} = \bigcup_{j=1}^k q_j P$ with the union disjoint.
Then $\{q_1, \dots, q_k\}$ is irredundant.
Indeed, if $q_j P \subseteq q_\ell P$ with $j \neq \ell$, then $q_j \in q_j P \cap q_\ell P = \emptyset$, which is absurd.
By the first part $s_i P = q_{\sigma(i)} P$ for all $i$, and therefore the family $\{ s_i P \}_{i=1}^m$ is pairwise disjoint.
The converse is trivial.

label: P:fafibres
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{P:fafibres}
Let $P$ be a unital subsemigroup of a discrete group $G$ and let $X$ be a saturated product system over $P$.
If $\emptyset \neq {\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$ is a finitely generated constructible ideal with irredundant generating family $\{p_1, \dots, p_m\}$, then the map
\[
\Phi_{{\mathbf{x}}} \colon \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, \lambda_\ast} \to \bigoplus_{i=1}^m {\mathcal{L}}(X_{p_i});\
b \mapsto \left( \operatorname{ev}_{p_1}(b), \dots, \operatorname{ev}_{p_m}(b) \right),
\]
is an injective $*$-homomorphism.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By item (i) of Lemma~\ref{L:fadiag} we have that $\Phi_{\mathbf{x}}$ is a $*$-homomorphism.
Suppose that $\Phi_{\mathbf{x}}(b) = 0$ and let $r$ be in ${\mathbf{x}}$.
Then $r = p_i s$ for some $i$ and some $s \in P$, and item (ii) of Lemma~\ref{L:fadiag} gives 
\[
\operatorname{ev}_r(b)=\operatorname{ev}_{p_i s}(b) = i_{p_i}^{p_i s}(\operatorname{ev}_{p_i}(b)) = 0.
\]
By item (i) of Lemma~\ref{L:fadiag} we conclude that $b = 0$.

label: D:fa
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{D:fa}
A unital subsemigroup $P$ of a discrete group $G$ is called \emph{finitely aligned} if $pP \cap qP$ is a finitely generated right ideal for all $p, q \in P$.
head: environment

label: Ex:fa
title: Example
body_md:
\label{Ex:fa}
Finitely aligned semigroups that are not right LCM semigroups are abundant.
For example, the numerical semigroup $P = \{0, 2, 3, 4, \dots\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ is finitely aligned, while
\[
(2 + P) \cap (3 + P) = \{5, 6, 7, \dots\} = (5+P) \cup (6+P)
\]
is not principal, and hence $P$ is not a right LCM semigroup.
head: environment

label: P:fajfg
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\noindent
[(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i)].
This is immediate, since $pP \cap qP \in {\mathcal{J}}$.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii)].
Write ${\mathcal{J}}_{\rm fg}$ for the family of finitely generated right ideals of $P$.
Clearly $P = e_P P \in {\mathcal{J}}_{\rm fg}$ and $\emptyset \in {\mathcal{J}}_{\rm fg}$.
Since ${\mathcal{J}}$ is the smallest family of right ideals of $P$ that contains $P$ and $\emptyset$ and is closed under the operations ${\mathbf{x}} \mapsto p {\mathbf{x}}$ and ${\mathbf{x}} \mapsto p^{-1}{\mathbf{x}}$ for $p \in P$, and under finite intersections, it suffices to check that ${\mathcal{J}}_{\rm fg}$ shares the same closure properties.

Fix ${\mathbf{x}} = \bigcup_{i=1}^m r_i P \in {\mathcal{J}}_{\rm fg}$ and $p \in P$.
Then $p {\mathbf{x}} = \bigcup_{i=1}^m (p r_i) P \in {\mathcal{J}}_{\rm fg}$.
For the second operation, note that $p^{-1} {\mathbf{x}} = \bigcup_{i=1}^m p^{-1}(r_i P)$, and since the union of finitely generated right ideals is finitely generated, we may assume that ${\mathbf{x}} = r P$ is principal.
By finite alignment write $p P \cap r P = \bigcup_{j=1}^n w_j P$, and for each $j$ let $u_j \in P$ be the unique element with $w_j = p u_j$.
For $x \in P$ we have
\[
p x \in r P
\iff
p x \in pP \cap rP
\iff
p x \in p u_j P \text{ for some } j
\iff
x \in u_j P \text{ for some } j.
\]
Hence $p^{-1}(rP) = \bigcup_{j=1}^n u_j P \in {\mathcal{J}}_{\rm fg}$.
Finally, if ${\mathbf{x}} = \bigcup_{i=1}^m r_i P$ and ${\mathbf{y}} = \bigcup_{j=1}^n s_j P$ are in ${\mathcal{J}}_{\rm fg}$, then ${\mathbf{x}} \cap {\mathbf{y}} = \bigcup_{i, j} \left( r_i P \cap s_j P \right)$, and each $r_i P \cap s_j P$ is finitely generated by finite alignment.
Thus ${\mathbf{x}} \cap {\mathbf{y}} \in {\mathcal{J}}_{\rm fg}$, and the proof is complete.

label: D:mcm
title: Definition
head: environment

label: D:famin
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{D:famin}
Let $P$ be a unital finitely aligned subsemigroup of a discrete group $G$.
A saturated product system $X$ over $P$ is called \emph{compactly aligned} if
\[
i_p^w(k_p) \, i_q^w(k_q) \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_w)
\text{ for all } k_p \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_p), k_q \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_q),
\]
for all $p, q \in P$ and every minimal common right multiple $w$ of $p$ and $q$.
head: environment

label: R:famin
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{R:famin}
By the discussion after \cite[Definition 2.9]{DKKLL22} we have that, if $w = zx$ for $x \in P^\ast$, then
\[
i_p^w(k_p) \, i_q^w(k_q) \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_w) 
\quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad
i_p^z(k_p) \, i_q^z(k_q) \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_z)
\]
for all $k_p \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_p)$ and $k_q \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_q)$.
Let $P$ be finitely aligned and let $\{w_1, \dots, w_m\}$ be an irredundant generating family for $pP \cap qP$.
By Lemma~\ref{L:famax} each $w_j$ is a minimal common right multiple of $p$ and $q$, and every element of $pP \cap qP$ lies in $w_j P$ for some $j$; hence every minimal common right multiple of $p$ and $q$ equals $w_j x$ for some $j$ and $x \in P^\ast$.
Therefore Definition~\ref{D:famin} reduces to the conditions at $w_1, \dots, w_m$, which by Lemma~\ref{L:fairr} do not depend on the choice of the irredundant family.

label: L:facomp
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{L:facomp}
Let $P$ be a unital finitely aligned subsemigroup of a discrete group $G$ and let $X$ be a compactly aligned saturated product system over $P$.
Let $u, v \in P$, let $w$ be a minimal common right multiple of $u$ and $v$, and write $w = u y_u = v y_v$ with $y_u, y_v \in P$.
Then
\[
i^{y_v}_{p,v} \left( {\mathcal{K}}(X_v, X_p) \right)
i^{y_u}_{u,q} \left( {\mathcal{K}}(X_q, X_u) \right)
\subseteq
{\mathcal{K}} \left( X_{q y_u}, X_{p y_v} \right)
\text{ for all } p, q \in P.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider $k_1 \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_q, X_u)$ and $k_2 \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_v, X_p)$, and set
\[
S_1 := i^{y_u}_{u,q}(k_1) \in {\mathcal{L}}(X_{q y_u}, X_w)
\quad\text{and}\quad
S_2 := i^{y_v}_{p,v}(k_2) \in {\mathcal{L}}(X_w, X_{p y_v}),
\]
where we used that $u y_u = w = v y_v$.
Let $(e_\iota)_\iota$ and $(e'_\kappa)_\kappa$ be contractive approximate units for ${\mathcal{K}}(X_u)$ and ${\mathcal{K}}(X_v)$ respectively.
Then we have $\lim_\iota e_\iota k_1 = k_1$ and $\lim_\kappa k_2 e'_\kappa = k_2$ in norm, and therefore, by items (i) and (iv) of Lemma~\ref{L:faj}, we get
\[
S_1 = \lim_\iota i^{y_u}_{u,q}(e_\iota k_1) = \lim_\iota i_u^{w}(e_\iota) \, S_1
\quad\text{and}\quad
S_2 = \lim_\kappa i^{y_v}_{p,v}(k_2 e'_\kappa) = \lim_\kappa S_2 \, i_v^{w}(e'_\kappa).
\]
We thus obtain
\[
S_2 S_1 = \lim_\kappa \lim_\iota S_2 \, i_v^w(e'_\kappa) \, i_u^w(e_\iota) \, S_1.
\]
Since $w$ is a minimal common right multiple of $u$ and $v$, by compact alignment of $X$ we obtain that $i_v^w(e'_\kappa) i_u^w(e_\iota) \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_w)$, and therefore
\[
S_2 \, i_v^w(e'_\kappa) \, i_u^w(e_\iota) \, S_1 \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_{q y_u}, X_{p y_v}) \text{ for all } \iota, \kappa.
\]
Since ${\mathcal{K}}(X_{q y_u}, X_{p y_v})$ is norm closed the same holds for $S_2 S_1$.

label: P:fanormal
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{P:fanormal}
Let $P$ be a unital finitely aligned subsemigroup of a discrete group $G$ and let $X$ be a compactly aligned saturated product system over $P$.
Let $p_1, q_1, \dots, p_n, q_n \in P$ and $\xi_{p_i} \in X_{p_i}, \xi_{q_i} \in X_{q_i}$ for $i = 1, \dots, n$, and consider 
\[
g := p_1^{-1} q_1 \cdots p_n^{-1} q_n \in G 
\ \text{ and } \
{\mathbf{x}} := q_n^{-1} p_n \dots q_1^{-1} p_1 P \in {\mathcal{J}},
\]
and an element of the form
\[
b := \lambda_{p_1}(\xi_{p_1})^* \lambda_{q_1}(\xi_{q_1}) \cdots
\lambda_{p_n}(\xi_{p_n})^* \lambda_{q_n}(\xi_{q_n}) \in {\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X).
\]
Then for every $r \in {\mathbf{x}}$ there exist $s \in {\mathbf{x}}$ and $z \in P$ with $r = s z$, and $S \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_s, X_{gs})$, such that
\[
b|_{X_r} = i^z_{gs, s}(S).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Given $r \in {\mathbf{x}}$ we shall produce $s$, $z$ and $S$, and verify the identity.
Note that once $s \in {\mathbf{x}}$ and $r = s z$ are given, we have $gs, gr \in P$ by Proposition~\ref{P:mult} and $gr = (gs)z$ in $G$, so that $i^z_{gs,s}$ maps ${\mathcal{L}}(X_s, X_{gs})$ into ${\mathcal{L}}(X_r, X_{gr})$, which is where $b|_{X_r}$ lives.
We induct on $n$.

\smallskip
\noindent
{\it Base case $n = 1$.}
Here $b = \lambda_{p_1}(\xi_{p_1})^* \lambda_{q_1}(\xi_{q_1})$, $g = p_1^{-1} q_1$ and ${\mathbf{x}} = q_1^{-1} p_1 P = \{ r \in P \mid q_1 r \in p_1 P \}$.
Fix $r \in {\mathbf{x}}$, so that $q_1 r \in p_1 P \cap q_1 P$.
By Remark~\ref{R:famin} we may choose a minimal common right multiple $w$ of $p_1$ and $q_1$ with $q_1 r \in wP$, and we write
\[
w = p_1 y_1 = q_1 y_2
\quad\text{and}\quad
q_1 r = w z
\text{ for } y_1, y_2, z \in P.
\]
From $q_1 r = q_1 y_2 z$ and left cancellation we get $r = y_2 z$.
Set $s := y_2$, so that $r = s z$ and $g s = p_1^{-1} q_1 y_2 = p_1^{-1} w = y_1$.
Moreover, we have $q_1 s = w \in p_1 P$ and hence $s \in {\mathbf{x}}$.
Set
\[
S := i^{y_1}_{e_P, p_1}
\left( \left( M^{e_P, p_1}_{\xi_{p_1}} \right)^* \right)
\, i^{y_2}_{q_1, e_P} \left( M^{e_P, q_1}_{\xi_{q_1}} \right),
\]
which lies in ${\mathcal{K}}(X_{y_2}, X_{y_1}) = {\mathcal{K}}(X_s, X_{gs})$ by Lemma~\ref{L:famult} and Lemma~\ref{L:facomp}, the latter applied with $u := q_1$, $v := p_1$, $y_u := y_2$, $y_v := y_1$ and $p = q := e_P$.
By Lemma~\ref{L:facreate} and item (iii) of Lemma~\ref{L:faj} we have
\[
\lambda_{q_1}(\xi_{q_1})|_{X_r}
=
i^{y_2 z}_{q_1, e_P} \left( M^{e_P,q_1}_{\xi_{q_1}} \right)
=
i^{z}_{w, y_2} \left( i^{y_2}_{q_1, e_P}
\left( M^{e_P,q_1}_{\xi_{q_1}} \right) \right),
\]
since $r = y_2 z$ and $q_1 y_2 = w$, and likewise
\[
\lambda_{p_1}(\xi_{p_1})^*|_{X_{q_1 r}}
=
i^{y_1 z}_{e_P, p_1}
\left( \left( M^{e_P,p_1}_{\xi_{p_1}} \right)^* \right)
=
i^{z}_{y_1, w} \left( i^{y_1}_{e_P, p_1}
\left( \left( M^{e_P,p_1}_{\xi_{p_1}} \right)^* \right) \right),
\]
since $q_1 r = w z = p_1 y_1 z$.
Composing and using item (ii) of Lemma~\ref{L:faj} we obtain
\[
b|_{X_r} = i^{z}_{y_1, y_2}(S) = i^z_{gs, s}(S).
\]

\smallskip
\noindent
{\it Inductive step.}
Let $n \geq 2$ and write $b = b' c$, where $c := \lambda_{p_n}(\xi_{p_n})^* \lambda_{q_n}(\xi_{q_n})$ and $b'$ is the word with parameters $p_1, q_1, \dots, p_{n-1}, q_{n-1}$.
Write
\[
h := p_n^{-1} q_n, \quad {\mathbf{y}} := q_n^{-1} p_n P
\quad\text{and}\quad
g' := p_1^{-1} q_1 \cdots p_{n-1}^{-1} q_{n-1}, \quad
{\mathbf{x}}' := q_{n-1}^{-1} p_{n-1} \dots q_1^{-1} p_1 P,
\]
for the data attached to $c$ and to $b'$, so that $g = g' h$ and
\[
{\mathbf{x}} = q_n^{-1} p_n {\mathbf{x}}' = \{ r \in {\mathbf{y}} \mid h r \in {\mathbf{x}}' \}.
\]
Fix $r \in {\mathbf{x}}$.
By the base case applied to $c$ at $r$ there are $s_1 \in {\mathbf{y}}$ and $z_1 \in P$ with $r = s_1 z_1$, and $S_1 \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_{s_1}, X_{u})$ with $u := h s_1$, such that $c|_{X_r} = i^{z_1}_{u, s_1}(S_1)$.
By the inductive hypothesis applied to $b'$ at $h r \in {\mathbf{x}}'$ there are $v \in {\mathbf{x}}'$ and $z' \in P$ with $h r = v z'$, and $S' \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_v, X_{g'v})$, such that $b'|_{X_{hr}} = i^{z'}_{g'v, v}(S')$.

Since $h r = u z_1 = v z'$ we have $h r \in u P \cap v P$, and by Remark~\ref{R:famin} we may choose a minimal common right multiple $w$ of $u$ and $v$ with $hr \in wP$.
Write $w = u y_u = v y_v$ and $h r = w z$ with $y_u, y_v, z \in P$.
From $u z_1 = u y_u z$ and left cancellation we get $z_1 = y_u z$, and likewise $z' = y_v z$.
Set
\[
s := s_1 y_u
\quad\text{and}\quad
S := i^{y_v}_{g'v, v}(S') \; i^{y_u}_{u, s_1}(S_1),
\]
so that 
\[
r = s_1 y_u z = s z
\text{ and } 
g s = g' h s_1 y_u = g' u y_u = g' w = g' v y_v,
\]
while $S \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_{s}, X_{gs})$ by Lemma~\ref{L:facomp} applied with $p := g'v$ and $q := s_1$.
By items (iii) and (ii) of Lemma~\ref{L:faj} we obtain
\begin{align*}
b|_{X_r}
&=
b'|_{X_{hr}} \circ c|_{X_r}
=
i^{z'}_{g'v, v}(S')
i^{z_1}_{u, s_1}(S_1)\\
&=
i^{y_v z}_{g'v, v}(S')
i^{y_u z}_{u, s_1}(S_1)
=
i^{z}_{g'w, w}\left( i^{y_v}_{g'v, v}(S') \right)
i^{z}_{w, s}\left( i^{y_u}_{u, s_1}(S_1) \right)
=
i^{z}_{gs, s}(S).
\end{align*}
Finally $s = s_1 y_u \in {\mathbf{y}}$, since $s_1 \in {\mathbf{y}}$ and ${\mathbf{y}}$ is a right ideal, while $h s = u y_u = w \in v P \subseteq {\mathbf{x}}'$, since $v \in {\mathbf{x}}'$ and ${\mathbf{x}}'$ is a right ideal.
Hence $s \in {\mathbf{x}}$ and the induction is complete.

label: C:facompact
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{C:facompact}
Let $P$ be a unital finitely aligned subsemigroup of a discrete group $G$ and let $X$ be a compactly aligned saturated product system over $P$.
Let $\emptyset \neq {\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$ with irredundant generating family $\{s_1, \dots, s_m\}$.
Then
\[
\operatorname{ev}_{s_i} \left( \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, \lambda_\ast} \right) \subseteq {\mathcal{K}}(X_{s_i})
\text{ for all } i = 1, \dots, m.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $i \in \{1, \dots, m\}$.
By Proposition~\ref{P:fanoeps} it suffices to consider an element $b\in \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast}$ of the form 
\[
b:=\lambda_{p_1}(\xi_{p_1})^*\lambda_{q_1}(\xi_{q_1}) \cdots \lambda_{p_n}(\xi_{p_n})^*\lambda_{q_n}(\xi_{q_n}) \text{ where } n\in \mathbb{N}, p_j,q_j \in P \text{ for all } j=1,\dots,n,
\]
such that $p_1^{-1} q_1\cdots p_n^{-1} q_n= e_P$ and $q_n^{-1}p_n\dots q_1^{-1}p_1P={\mathbf{x}}$, since the linear span of such elements is dense in $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, \lambda_\ast}$.
Proposition~\ref{P:fanormal} applied at $s_i \in {\mathbf{x}}$ provides $s \in {\mathbf{x}}$ and $z \in P$ with $s_i = s z$, and $S \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_s)$, such that $\operatorname{ev}_{s_i}(b) = i^z_{s,s}(S)$.
Since $s_i \in s P$ and $s \in {\mathbf{x}}$, Lemma~\ref{L:famax} gives $z \in P^*$, and therefore
\[
\operatorname{ev}_{s_i}(b) = i^z_{s,s}(S) \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_{sz}) = {\mathcal{K}}(X_{s_i}),
\]
by item (ii) of Lemma~\ref{L:faunits}.
The claim follows, since $\operatorname{ev}_{s_i}$ is contractive and ${\mathcal{K}}(X_{s_i})$ is closed.
head: environment

label: R:faneed
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{R:faneed}
Compact alignment is used in an essential way in Proposition~\ref{P:fanormal}, as the conclusion of Corollary~\ref{C:facompact} fails without this assumption.

For an example, consider the finitely aligned semigroup $P = \{0, 2, 3, 4, \dots\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and let $H$ be an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space.
We may regard $Y:=H$ as a non-degenerate C*-correspondence over $A:=\mathbb{C}$.
Setting $X_p := Y^{\otimes p}$ for $p \in P$ defines a saturated product system over $P$ with connecting maps $u_{p,q}$ given by the associativity of the stabilised tensor product.
Take 
\[
{\mathbf{x}} := (2+P) \cap (3+P) = \{5,6,7,\dots\},
\]
so that $\{5,6\}$ is an irredundant generating family for ${\mathbf{x}}$ by Example~\ref{Ex:fa}, and consider
\[
b
:=
\lambda^{(2)}(\theta^{X_2}_{\xi, \eta}) \,
\lambda^{(3)}(\theta^{X_3}_{\zeta, \omega})
\in \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, \lambda_\ast}
\textup{ for }
\xi, \eta \in X_2, \ \zeta, \omega \in X_3.
\]
Since $5 = 2 + 3 = 3 + 2$, Lemma~\ref{L:fadiag} and Lemma~\ref{L:facptfibre} give
\[
\operatorname{ev}_5(b) =\operatorname{ev}_5(\lambda^{(2)}(\theta^{X_2}_{\xi, \eta})) \operatorname{ev}_5(\lambda^{(3)}(\theta^{X_3}_{\zeta, \omega}))= i_2^5 \left( \theta^{X_2}_{\xi,\eta} \right) \, i_3^5 \left( \theta^{X_3}_{\zeta,\omega} \right).
\]
Consider $\zeta = \zeta_1 \otimes \zeta_2$ with $\zeta_1 \in Y^{\otimes 2}$ and $\zeta_2 \in Y$, and set $\mu := \xi \left\langle\eta, \zeta_1\right\rangle \otimes \zeta_2 \in X_3$.
We will show that
\begin{equation}\label{Eq:comp5}
\operatorname{ev}_5(b) \nu = i_3^5 \left( \theta^{X_3}_{\mu, \omega} \right) \nu
\text{ for all } \nu \in X_5.
\end{equation}
For $\mu \neq 0$ (for example by choosing $\xi=\eta=\zeta_1 \neq 0$ and $\zeta_2 \neq 0$) and $\omega \neq 0$, we will get 
\[
\operatorname{ev}_5(b) 
= 
i_3^5 \left( \theta^{X_3}_{\mu, \omega} \right)
=
\theta^{X_3}_{\mu, \omega} \otimes {\operatorname{id}}_{Y^{\otimes 2}}
\notin {\mathcal{K}}(X_5),
\]
as $Y^{\otimes 2}$ is infinite-dimensional.
Hence the conclusion of Corollary~\ref{C:facompact} fails for this product system.
Moreover we will get that $X$ is not compactly aligned since
\[
i_2^5({\mathcal{K}}(X_2)) \, i_3^5({\mathcal{K}}(X_3)) \not\subseteq {\mathcal{K}}(X_5).
\]

For \eqref{Eq:comp5}, it suffices to consider $\nu = \nu_1 \otimes \nu_2$ with $\nu_1 \in X_3$ and $\nu_2 \in X_2$.
In this case we have
\begin{align*}
\operatorname{ev}_5(b) \nu
& =
i_2^5 \left( \theta^{X_2}_{\xi,\eta} \right) \, i_3^5 \left( \theta^{X_3}_{\zeta,\omega} \right) (\nu_1 \otimes \nu_2)
=
i_2^5 \left( \theta^{X_2}_{\xi,\eta} \right) \left(\zeta_1 \otimes (\zeta_2 \left\langle\omega,\nu_1\right\rangle) \otimes \nu_2\right) \\
& =
(\xi \left\langle\eta, \zeta_1\right\rangle) \otimes (\zeta_2 \left\langle\omega,\nu_1\right\rangle) \otimes \nu_2
=
(\mu \left\langle\omega, \nu_1\right\rangle) \otimes \nu_2
=
i_3^5 \left( \theta^{X_3}_{\mu, \omega} \right) \nu,
\end{align*}
as required.

label: P:famain
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For ${\mathbf{x}} = \emptyset$ we have $\mathbf{K}_{\emptyset, \lambda_\ast} = (0)$ by \eqref{Eq:faKempty}, and there is nothing to prove.
So consider $\emptyset \neq {\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$.
By Proposition~\ref{P:fajfg} we may fix an irredundant generating family $\{p_1, \dots, p_m\}$ for ${\mathbf{x}}$.
By Proposition~\ref{P:fafibres} the map 
\[
\Phi_{{\mathbf{x}}} \colon \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, \lambda_\ast} \to \bigoplus_{i=1}^m {\mathcal{L}}(X_{p_i});
\
b \mapsto \left( \operatorname{ev}_{p_1}(b), \dots, \operatorname{ev}_{p_m}(b) \right),
\]
is an injective $*$-homomorphism, and by Corollary~\ref{C:facompact} we obtain that its range is actually contained in $\bigoplus_{i=1}^m {\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i})$.
Hence $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, \lambda_\ast}$ is $*$-isomorphic to a C*-subalgebra of $\bigoplus_{i=1}^m {\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i})$.
Each ${\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i})$ is exact by \cite[Proposition B.7]{Kat04}, a finite direct sum of exact C*-algebras is exact, and exactness passes to C*-subalgebras.
Therefore $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, \lambda_\ast}$ is exact.

title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\noindent
[(i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii)].
Proposition~\ref{P:famain} implies that $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, \lambda_\ast}$ is exact for every ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$ and hence ${\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)$ is exact by applying Corollary~\ref{C:Excores-3}.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i)].
This is immediate as $\lambda$ is injective and exactness passes to C*-subalgebras.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(ii) $\Leftrightarrow$ (iii)].
This is Corollary~\ref{C:Excores-2}.

title: Definition
body_md: A unital subsemigroup $P$ of a discrete group $G$ is called \emph{strongly finitely aligned} if for every $p,q \in P$ the constructible ideal $pP\cap qP$ can be written as a disjoint union of finitely many principal right ideals of $P$.
head: environment

label: P:sfa
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\noindent
[(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i)].
This is immediate, since $pP \cap qP \in {\mathcal{J}}$.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii)].
If ${\mathbf{x}}=\emptyset$ the conclusion holds trivially, so fix a non-empty ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$.
In this case ${\mathbf{x}}=q_n^{-1}p_n \dots q_1^{-1}p_1 P$ for some $n \geq 1$ and $p_i, q_i \in P$.
We proceed by induction on $n \geq 1$.
If $n=1$, then ${\mathbf{x}}=q_1^{-1}p_1 P=q_1^{-1}(p_1P \cap q_1P)$.
Since ${\mathbf{x}} \neq \emptyset$ we get that $p_1P \cap q_1P \neq \emptyset$ and hence item (i) implies that
\[
p_1P \cap q_1P = \bigcup_{j=1}^{m} s_jP \text{ for some } m \in \mathbb{N}, s_1, \dots, s_m \in P, \textup{ such that } s_i P \cap s_j P = \emptyset \text{ for } i \neq j.
\]
Since $P$ is unital we have $s_j \in q_1P$, say $s_j = q_1 t_j$ with $t_j \in P$.
It follows that
\[
t_iP \cap t_jP = q_1^{-1}(s_iP \cap s_j P) = \emptyset, \textup{ when } i \neq j,
\]
and moreover we get
\[
q_1^{-1}(p_1P) = q_1^{-1}(p_1P \cap q_1 P) = \bigcup_{j=1}^{m} t_jP.
\]
Now set ${\mathbf{x}}_0 := P$ and ${\mathbf{x}}_k := q_k^{-1}p_k {\mathbf{x}}_{k-1}$ for $k = 1, \dots, n$, so that ${\mathbf{x}} = {\mathbf{x}}_n$.
Suppose that
${\mathbf{x}}_{k-1} = \bigcup_{i=1}^{m} r_iP$ for some $r_1, \dots, r_m \in P$ where the union is disjoint.
Left cancellation gives $p_k{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1} = \bigcup_{i=1}^{m} p_kr_iP$.
Since preimages of disjoint sets are disjoint, we obtain
\[
{\mathbf{x}}_k = q_k^{-1}(p_k{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1}) = \bigcup_{i=1}^{m} q_k^{-1}(p_kr_iP),
\]
where the union is disjoint.
The case $n=1$ applied to $q_k$ and $p_kr_i$ yields that each $q_k^{-1}(p_kr_iP)$ is a disjoint union of finitely many principal right ideals.
Hence so is ${\mathbf{x}}_k$, which completes the induction.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
If $P$ is a semigroup such that any two principal right ideals of $P$ intersect, then a disjoint decomposition of $\emptyset \neq {\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$ into principal right ideals must consist of a single ideal.
Therefore in this case $P$ is strongly finitely aligned if and only if it is a right LCM semigroup.
This occurs for example when $P$ is commutative, or right Ore.

Another example is provided by semigroups with an independent set of constructible ideals.
Recall that ${\mathcal{J}}$ is called \emph{independent} if ${\mathbf{x}} = \bigcup_{i=1}^n {\mathbf{x}}_i$ with ${\mathbf{x}}, {\mathbf{x}}_1, \dots, {\mathbf{x}}_n \in {\mathcal{J}}$ implies ${\mathbf{x}} = {\mathbf{x}}_i$ for some $i$, see \cite{Li12}.
If $P$ is strongly finitely aligned and ${\mathcal{J}}$ is independent, then $P$ is again a right LCM semigroup.
Indeed, writing ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$ as a disjoint union $\bigcup_{i=1}^n p_i P$ with $n \geq 2$ would give ${\mathbf{x}} = p_i P$ for some $i$ by independence, contradicting the disjointness (as $p_j \in {\mathbf{x}} \setminus p_i P$ for $j \neq i$).
Hence every ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$ is empty or principal.
head: environment

label: E:BS
title: Example
body_md:
\label{E:BS}
For an example of a strongly finitely aligned semigroup that is not a right LCM semigroup and is embeddable in an amenable discrete group consider first the Baumslag--Solitar group $\mathrm{BS}(1,2)$.
This group has an affine realisation generated by
\[
a(s)=2s
\quad\text{and}\quad
b(s)=s+1,
\]
from which it follows that $\mathrm{BS}(1,2)\simeq \mathbb{Z}[1/2]\rtimes\mathbb{Z}$, and thus it is amenable.

Moreover, it is well known that the semigroup homomorphism
\[
\rho \colon \mathbb{F}_2^+ \to \mathrm{BS}(1,2); \ x \mapsto a, y \mapsto ba,
\]
is injective.
Indeed, set $t_0 := \rho(x) = a$ and $t_1 := \rho(y) = ba$, so that $t_0(s) = 2s$ and $t_1(s) = 2s+1$, and note that $\rho(w_1 \cdots w_n) = \rho(w_1) \circ \cdots \circ \rho(w_n)$ for $w_i \in \{x,y\}$.
For $\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_n\in\{0,1\}$, a product of these elements in the affine realisation has the form
\[
t_{\varepsilon_1}\cdots t_{\varepsilon_n}(s)
=2^ns+k,
\]
where $k = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \varepsilon_i 2^{i-1}$, as follows by induction on $n$.
Since $0 \leq k < 2^n$, the uniqueness of the binary expansion shows that the affine map $s \mapsto 2^n s + k$ determines both $n$ and the word $\varepsilon_1\cdots\varepsilon_n$.
Hence $\mathbb{F}_2^+ \hookrightarrow \mathrm{BS}(1,2)$.

It remains to identify a strongly finitely aligned subsemigroup of $\mathbb{F}_2^+$ that is not a right LCM semigroup.
Towards this end, let $P$ be the unital subsemigroup of $\mathbb{F}_2^+$ generated by $\{x, xy, yx, yyx\}$.
We record an observation that we will use repeatedly.
The generating set is not a prefix code, as $x$ is a prefix of $xy$, and so factorisations in $P$ need not be unique.
However, if a non-empty $w \in P$ begins with $y$, then the leading generator of any factorisation of $w$ is $yx$ or $yyx$, and it is determined by the second letter of $w$; consequently
\begin{equation} \label{Eq:BSlead}
w \in P \text{ begins with } y
\quad \Longrightarrow \quad
w \in yxP \cup yyxP,
\end{equation}
and no element of $P$ begins with $yyy$.
In particular, since $yx \in P$, for every $u \in \mathbb{F}_2^+$ we have
\begin{equation} \label{Eq:BScancel}
yxu \in P
\quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad
u \in P,
\end{equation}
where the forward implication follows from \eqref{Eq:BSlead} and left cancellation.

First we see that $P$ is finitely aligned.
For $w \in \mathbb{F}_2^+$ set
\[
P_w := \{ v \in P \mid w v \in P \}.
\]
Let $p,q\in P$.
We say that $p$ and $q$ are \emph{prefix-comparable} if there is a $w \in \mathbb{F}_2^+$ such that $q=pw$ or $p=qw$.
Since $P$ is contained in the free semigroup $\mathbb{F}_2^+$, if $p$ and $q$ are prefix-incomparable, then no word can have both $p$ and $q$ as prefixes, and hence $pP\cap qP=\emptyset$.
Suppose that $p$ and $q$ are prefix-comparable and, without loss of generality, that $q = pw$ for the unique $w \in \mathbb{F}_2^+$ with this property.
An element of $qP$ has the form $qv = pwv$ with $v \in P$, and it lies in $pP$ if and only if $wv \in P$.
Therefore
\begin{equation} \label{Eq:BSint}
pP \cap qP = q P_w,
\end{equation}
so that $pP \cap qP$ is determined by $q$ and by the word $w$ alone.
We claim that
\[
P_w = P
\quad \text{ or } \quad
P_w = \emptyset
\quad \text{ or } \quad
P_w = xP \cup yxP.
\]
In particular, the conclusion does not depend on the factorisations of $p$ and $q$ in $P$, which enter only in locating $w$.
Indeed, fix a factorisation $q = g_1 \cdots g_n$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $g_i \in \{x, xy, yx, yyx\}$.
We have the following cases.

\smallskip
\noindent
{\it Case 1.}
If $p = g_1 \cdots g_m$ for some $m \leq n$, then $w = g_{m+1} \cdots g_n \in P$ and thus $P_w = P$.

\smallskip
\noindent
{\it Case 2.} Otherwise $p = g_1 \cdots g_m \alpha$ for some $m < n$, where $g_{m+1} = \alpha \beta$ with $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{F}_2^+$ non-empty, and $w = \beta g_{m+2} \cdots g_n$.
In particular, we get that $\beta \in \{x, y, yx\}$.

\begin{list}{}{ 
  \setlength{\leftmargin}{.5em} 
  \setlength{\itemindent}{0pt} 
  \setlength{\listparindent}{0pt} 
  \setlength{\parsep}{\smallskipamount} 
  \setlength{\itemsep}{\smallskipamount} 
  \setlength{\topsep}{\smallskipamount}}
\item[--] {\it Case 2a.}
If $\beta \in \{x, yx\}$, then $w \in P$ and thus $P_w = P$.

\item[--] {\it Case 2b.}
If $\beta = y$, then $w = y z_1 \cdots z_\ell$, for $\ell := n-m-1$ and $z_i := g_{m+1+i}$.
We show by induction on $\ell \geq 0$ that $P_{y z_1 \cdots z_\ell}$ is one of $P$, $\emptyset$ or $xP \cup yxP$, for all $z_1, \dots, z_\ell \in \{x, xy, yx, yyx\}$.

For $\ell = 0$ we have $w = y$.
If $v \in P_y$, then $yv \in P$ begins with $y$, and so $yv \in yxP \cup yyxP$ by \eqref{Eq:BSlead}; cancelling $y$ gives $v \in xP \cup yxP$.
Conversely $y \cdot xP = yxP \subseteq P$ and $y \cdot yxP = yyxP \subseteq P$.
Hence $P_y = xP \cup yxP$.

For $\ell \geq 1$ we distinguish according to $z_1$.
If $z_1 \in \{x, yx\}$, then $y z_1 \in \{yx, yyx\}$ is a generator, so $w = (y z_1) z_2 \cdots z_\ell \in P$ and thus $P_w = P$.
If $z_1 = yyx$, then $w$ begins with $yyy$, and so does $wv$ for every $v \in P$; since no element of $P$ begins with $yyy$, we get $P_w = \emptyset$.
If $z_1 = xy$, then $w = yx \cdot w'$ for $w' := y z_2 \cdots z_\ell$, and \eqref{Eq:BScancel} gives
\[
v \in P_w
\iff
w' v \in P
\iff
v \in P_{w'},
\]
that is $P_w = P_{w'}$, and the inductive hypothesis applies to $w'$.
\end{list}

For strong finite alignment, it remains only to check that the unions $qxP \cup qyxP$ are disjoint.
Indeed, if $qxu=qyxv$ for some $u,v\in P$, cancellation of $q$ in the free semigroup gives $xu=yxv$, which is impossible because the word on the left begins with $x$ and the word on the right begins with $y$.
Thus $qxP\cap qyxP=\emptyset$, as required.

In order to see that $P$ is not a right LCM semigroup, we apply the above to $p := x$ and $q := xy$, so that $w = y$ and
\[
xP\cap xyP
=
xyxP \cup xyyxP.
\]
This intersection is not principal.
Indeed, if it equalled $zP$ for some $z \in P$, then $z \in zP$ would give $z \in xyxP \cup xyyxP$ and hence $|z| \geq 3$, while $xyx, xyyx \in zP$ would force $z$ to be a prefix of both $xyx$ and $xyyx$, whose longest common prefix is $xy$; thus $|z| \leq 2$, a contradiction.
Hence the semigroup $P$ is not a right LCM semigroup, as required.

label: P:facore
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{P:facore}
Let $P$ be a unital finitely aligned subsemigroup of a discrete group $G$ and let $X$ be a compactly aligned saturated product system over $P$.
Let $\emptyset \neq {\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$ and suppose that ${\mathbf{x}} = \bigcup_{i=1}^m p_i P$ with $p_i P \cap p_j P = \emptyset$ for all $i \neq j$.
Then
\[
\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, \lambda_\ast}
\subseteq
\sum_{i=1}^m \lambda^{(p_i)}({\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i})).
\]
If in addition $t$ is a Fock covariant representation of $X$, then
\[
\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, t_\ast}
\subseteq
\sum_{i=1}^m t^{(p_i)}({\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i})).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Disjointness of the union implies that the family $\{p_1, \dots, p_m\}$ is irredundant.
Indeed, if $p_i P \subseteq p_j P$ for some $i,j$, then $p_i \in p_i P \cap p_j P $ and thus $i=j$.
Hence Corollary~\ref{C:facompact} yields
\[
k_i := \operatorname{ev}_{p_i}(b) \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i})
\text{ for all } b \in \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, \lambda_\ast}, \ i = 1, \dots, m.
\]

Fix $b \in \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, \lambda_\ast}$ and set $c := \sum_{i=1}^m \lambda^{(p_i)}(k_i)$.
By item (i) of Lemma~\ref{L:fadiag} and Lemma~\ref{L:facptfibre}, both $b$ and $c$ leave every fibre $X_r$ invariant. Since ${\mathcal{F}} X = \sum^\oplus_{r \in P} X_r$ it therefore suffices to show that $\operatorname{ev}_r(b) = \operatorname{ev}_r(c)$ for every $r \in P$.

If $r \notin {\mathbf{x}}$, then $\operatorname{ev}_r(b) = 0$ by item (i) of Lemma~\ref{L:fadiag}, while $r \notin p_i P$ for every $i$ and hence $\operatorname{ev}_r(c) = 0$ by Lemma~\ref{L:facptfibre}.
If $r \in {\mathbf{x}}$, then by disjointness there is exactly one index $i$ with $r \in p_i P$.
Writing $r = p_i z$ with $z \in P$ we obtain
\[
\operatorname{ev}_r(c)
=
i_{p_i}^{p_i z} (k_i)
=
i_{p_i}^{p_i z} \left( \operatorname{ev}_{p_i}(b) \right)
=
\operatorname{ev}_{p_i z}(b)
=
\operatorname{ev}_r(b),
\]
where the first equality follows from Lemma~\ref{L:facptfibre} together with $\operatorname{ev}_r(\lambda^{(p_j)}(k_j)) = 0$ for $j \neq i$, and the third equality is item (ii) of Lemma~\ref{L:fadiag}.
Hence $b = c$, which proves the first assertion.

For the second assertion, let $\dot{t} \colon [{\mathcal{F}}{\mathcal{C}} X]_{e_P} \to \mathrm{C}^*(t)$ be the canonically induced $*$-homomorphism by the Fock covariance of $t$.
Since $\lambda^{(p)}({\mathcal{K}} (X_p))\subseteq [{\mathcal{F}}{\mathcal{C}} X]_{e_P}$ and $\mathbf{K}_{\mathbf{x}, \lambda_\ast} \subseteq [{\mathcal{F}}{\mathcal{C}} X]_{e_P}$, it follows that $\dot{t} \circ \lambda^{(p)} = t^{(p)}$ and $\dot{t}(\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, \lambda_\ast}) = \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, t_\ast}$.
Applying $\dot{t}$ to the first assertion finishes the proof.

label: P:fadirect
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{P:fadirect}
Let $P$ be a unital subsemigroup of a discrete group $G$ and let $X$ be a saturated product system over $P$.
Let $p_1, \dots, p_m \in P$ satisfy $p_i P \cap p_j P = \emptyset$ for $i \neq j$.
Then
\[
\lambda^{(p_i)}({\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i})) \cdot \lambda^{(p_j)}({\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_j})) = (0)
\text{ for all } i \neq j.
\]
If in addition $t$ is an equivariant Fock covariant representation of $X$, then 
\[
t^{(p_i)}({\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i})) \cdot t^{(p_j)}({\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_j})) = (0) 
\text{ for all } i \neq j,
\]
and consequently
\[
\sum_{i=1}^m t^{(p_i)}({\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i}))
=
\bigoplus_{i=1}^m t^{(p_i)}({\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i}))
\]
is a C*-subalgebra of $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $i \neq j$, and consider $k \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i})$ and $k' \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_j})$.
Let also $\zeta_r$ be in $X_r$ for some $r \in P$.
If $r \notin p_j P$, then Lemma~\ref{L:facptfibre} implies that $\lambda^{(p_j)}(k') \zeta_r = 0$.
If $r \in p_j P$, then $\lambda^{(p_j)}(k') \zeta_r \in X_r$ by the same lemma, while $r \notin p_i P$ by disjointness, and therefore $\lambda^{(p_i)}(k) \lambda^{(p_j)}(k') \zeta_r = 0$.
Since ${\mathcal{F}} X = \sum^\oplus_{r \in P} X_r$ we conclude that $\lambda^{(p_i)}(k) \lambda^{(p_j)}(k') = 0$.

Now let $t$ be an equivariant Fock covariant representation of $X$ and let $\dot{t} \colon [{\mathcal{F}}{\mathcal{C}} X]_{e_P} \to \mathrm{C}^*(t)$ be the canonically induced $*$-homomorphism so that $\dot{t} \circ \lambda^{(p)} = t^{(p)}$.
Applying $\dot{t}$ gives 
\[
t^{(p_i)}(k) t^{(p_j)}(k') = 0 \text{ for any }i \neq j.
\]
In particular the C*-algebras $t^{(p_i)}({\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i}))$ are mutually orthogonal C*-subalgebras of $\mathrm{C}^*(t)$, and hence the sum $\sum_{i=1}^m t^{(p_i)}({\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i}))$ is a direct sum and a C*-subalgebra of $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$ as each $t^{(p_i)}({\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i})) \subseteq [\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$.
