body_md:
\noindent 
[(ii) $\Leftrightarrow$ (iii)].
This follows from Theorem~\ref{T:Nuccores}.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i)].
Taking $n = 1$, $p_1 = q_1 = e_P$ and $\varepsilon = \varepsilon' = 1$ in the definition of the $\mathbf{K}$-cores we get $p_1^{-1} q_1 = e_P$ and $q_1^{-1} p_1 P = P$, and therefore
\[
t_{e_P}(A) = \left[ t_{e_P}(A)^* t_{e_P}(A) \right] \subseteq
\mathbf{K}_{P, t_\ast}.
\]
Since $t$ is injective we may identify $A$ with $t_{e_P}(A)$, and the inclusion of $A$ in $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$ is nuclear, since it factors as 
$A \hookrightarrow \mathbf{K}_{P, t_\ast} \hookrightarrow [\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$.

\smallskip
\noindent
[(i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii)].
Fix ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$.
If ${\mathbf{x}}=\emptyset$, then $\mathbf{K}_{\emptyset,t_\ast}=(0)$, and there is nothing to prove.
So suppose that ${\mathbf{x}}\neq \emptyset$.
Since $P$ is strongly finitely aligned, by Proposition~\ref{P:sfa} we may write
\[
{\mathbf{x}} = \bigcup_{i=1}^m p_i P \text{ with } p_i P \cap p_j P = \emptyset \text{ for all } i \neq j.
\]
Set ${\mathcal{C}} := \sum_{i=1}^m t^{(p_i)}({\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i}))$.
Since $t$ is injective, we get that $t^{(p)}$ is isometric for all $p\in P$, and hence nuclear embeddability of $t_{e_P}(A)$ in $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$ implies nuclear embeddability of each $t^{(p_i)}({\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i}))$ in $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$ by \cite[Proposition B.8]{Kat04}.
By Proposition~\ref{P:fadirect} the $t^{(p_i)}({\mathcal{K}}(X_{p_i}))$ are mutually orthogonal C*-subalgebras of $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$, and thus in turn ${\mathcal{C}}$ embeds nuclearly in $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$.
By Proposition~\ref{P:facore} we have that $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, t_\ast}$ is a C*-subalgebra of ${\mathcal{C}}$ and hence the inclusion map of $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, t_\ast}$ in $[\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$ is nuclear since it factors as
$\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, t_\ast} \hookrightarrow {\mathcal{C}} \hookrightarrow [\mathrm{C}^*(t)]_{e_P}$.

label: C:fanuc
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\noindent
The Fock representation is injective, equivariant and Fock covariant.
If $A$ is nuclear, then $\lambda_{e_P}(A)$ is a nuclear C*-subalgebra of $[{\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)]_{e_P}$, hence nuclearly embedded in it, and Theorem~\ref{T:fanuc} applies.

For the converse, consider the completely contractive completely positive map
\[
\operatorname{ev}_{e_P} \colon {\mathcal{L}}({\mathcal{F}} X) \to {\mathcal{L}}(X_{e_P}) = {\mathcal{L}}(A);\
c \mapsto Q_{e_P} c |_{X_{e_P}}.
\]
It is easy to check that $\operatorname{ev}_{e_P}$ restricts to a completely contractive completely positive map $\operatorname{ev}_{e_P}|_{{\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)} \colon {\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X) \to A$ satisfying $\operatorname{ev}_{e_P}|_{{\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)} \circ \lambda_{e_P} = {\operatorname{id}}_A$.
If ${\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)$ is nuclear, then evidently $\lambda_{e_P} \colon A \to {\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)$ is nuclear.
Hence we have that ${\operatorname{id}}_A = \operatorname{ev}_{e_P}|_{{\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)} \circ \lambda_{e_P}$ is nuclear, as required.

label: E:nonexact
title: Example
body_md:
\label{E:nonexact}
Below we obtain a product system over $\mathbb{Z}_+^2$ (hence over a right LCM semigroup) that is not compactly aligned, with $A = \mathbb{C}$ (hence exact), and we will have an ${\mathbf{x}} \in {\mathcal{J}}$ so that $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}}, \lambda_\ast}$ contains a copy of $\mathrm{C}^*(\mathbb{F}_2)$ (hence a non-exact C*-subalgebra).
This will show that compact alignment cannot be dropped from Theorem~\ref{T:faexact}, and as nuclearity implies exactness, nor can it be dropped from Theorem~\ref{T:fanuc}.
In addition, this example shows that the assumption of the left actions containing the compacts is also necessary for \cite[Theorem 5.4, Theorem 5.6]{KLS25}.

Let $H$ be a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space with orthonormal basis $\{h_j\}_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$.
Set $E = F := H$ and let $u \colon F \otimes E \to E \otimes F$ be any unitary; then $u$ is automatically a unitary for the C*-correspondences over $\mathbb{C}$, and $E$ and $F$ are non-degenerate.
We consider the saturated product system $X$ over $\mathbb{Z}_+^2$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{C}$, such that
\[
X_{(1,0)} = E, \quad X_{(0,1)} = F, \quad X_{(1,1)} = E \otimes F, \quad
u_{(1,0),(0,1)} = {\operatorname{id}}_{E \otimes F}, \quad u_{(0,1),(1,0)} = u.
\]
For $e \in E$ and $f \in F$ consider 
\[
L_e \colon F \to E \otimes F;\ L_e f' = e \otimes f'
\quad\text{and}\quad 
M_f \colon E \to F \otimes E ;\ M_f e' = f \otimes e'.
\]
By Lemma~\ref{L:facptfibre} we have
\[
\operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}\big(\lambda^{(1,0)}(k)\big) = k \otimes {\operatorname{id}}_F
\text{ for all } k \in {\mathcal{K}}(E),
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}\big(\lambda^{(0,1)}(\theta^{F}_{f,f'})\big) 
= u (\theta^F_{f,f'} \otimes {\operatorname{id}}_E) u^*
= u M_f M_{f'}^* u^*
\text{ for all } f,f' \in F.
\]
 
Consider the constructible ideal
\[
{\mathbf{x}} := (1,1) + \mathbb{Z}^2_+ = ((1,0)+\mathbb{Z}^2_+) \cap ((0,1)+\mathbb{Z}^2_+).
\]
Since $\lambda$ is a representation of $X$ we have
\[
\lambda_{(1,0)}(h_1)^*\lambda_{(1,0)}(h_1)=\lambda_{(0,0)}(\left\langleh_1,h_1\right\rangle)=1,
\]
and thus the element
\[
Q := \lambda^{(1,0)}(\theta^E_{h_1,h_1}) = \lambda_{(1,0)}(h_1) \lambda_{(1,0)}(h_1)^* \in \mathbf{K}_{(1,0)+\mathbb{Z}^2_+, \lambda_\ast}
\]
is a projection.
For $h_i, h_j \in F$ we define
\[
c_{ij} := Q \, \lambda^{(0,1)}(\theta^F_{h_i,h_j}) \, Q,
\]
for which we get
\[
c_{ij} = Q \, \lambda^{(0,1)}(\theta^F_{h_i,h_j}) \, Q \in \mathbf{K}_{(1,0)+\mathbb{Z}^2_+, \lambda_\ast} \cdot \mathbf{K}_{(0,1)+\mathbb{Z}^2_+, \lambda_\ast} \cdot \mathbf{K}_{(1,0)+\mathbb{Z}^2_+, \lambda_\ast}\subseteq \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast}.
\]
Since $Q$ is a projection we have
\[
c_{ij}=Qc_{ij}Q \in Q \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast} Q.
\]
Moreover, since $Q \in \mathbf{K}_{(1,0)+\mathbb{Z}^2_+, \lambda_\ast}$ and $((1,0)+\mathbb{Z}^2_+) \cap {\mathbf{x}} = {\mathbf{x}}$, we have
\[
Q \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast} Q
\subseteq 
\mathbf{K}_{(1,0)+\mathbb{Z}^2_+, \lambda_\ast} \cdot \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast} \cdot \mathbf{K}_{(1,0)+\mathbb{Z}^2_+, \lambda_\ast} \subseteq \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast},
\]
and therefore
\[
Q \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast} Q = \{ c \in \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast} \mid c = QcQ \}.
\]
It follows that $Q \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast} Q$ is a C*-subalgebra of $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast}$.
Since ${\mathbf{x}} = (1,1)+\mathbb{Z}^2_+$ is singly generated, Proposition~\ref{P:fafibres} implies that the map
\[
\operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}|_{\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast}} \colon \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast} \to {\mathcal{L}}(X_{(1,1)}) = {\mathcal{L}}(E \otimes F),
\]
is an injective $*$-homomorphism.
 
Henceforth we fix the isometry
\[
V := L_{h_1} \colon F \to E \otimes F;\ Vh = h_1 \otimes h.
\]
For its range projection $VV^*$ we have
\[
V V^* = \theta^E_{h_1,h_1} \otimes {\operatorname{id}}_F= \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(Q).
\]
Since $\operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}$ is a unital completely positive map on ${\mathcal{L}}({\mathcal{F}} X)$ and the operators $Q$ and $\operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(Q)$ are projections, we get
\[
\operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(Q^* Q)= \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(Q) = \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(Q)^* \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(Q),
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(Q Q^*)= \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(Q) = \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(Q) \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(Q)^*.
\]
Hence $Q$ lies in the multiplicative domain of $\operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}$.
Therefore, for every $c \in Q \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast} Q$ we have
\[
\operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(c) =\operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(QcQ) = \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(Q)\, \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(c)\, \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(Q) = V V^* \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(c)\, V V^*,
\]
and so $\operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(c) = V \Psi(c) V^*$, where
\[
\Psi \colon Q \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast} Q \to {\mathcal{B}}(F);\ 
c \mapsto V^* \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(c) V.
\]
A direct calculation for $c \in Q \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast} Q$ gives
\begin{align*}
VV^* \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(c) 
& = \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(Q) \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(c) 
= \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(c) \\
& = \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(c) \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(Q) 
= \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(c) V V^*,
\end{align*}
and so $\Psi$ is a $*$-homomorphism.
Finally, $\Psi$ is injective since $\operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(c) = V \Psi(c) V^*$, and $\operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}$ is injective on $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast} \supseteq Q \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast} Q$ by Proposition~\ref{P:fafibres}.
We conclude that $\Psi$ is an injective $*$-homomor\-phism which satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{Eq:psi}
\Psi(c_{ij}) 
= V^* \operatorname{ev}_{(1,1)}(c_{ij})V
= V^* u M_{h_i} M_{h_j}^* u^* V
= (V^* u M_{h_i})(V^* u M_{h_j})^*.
\end{equation}
 
The above hold for any separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space $H$ and any unitary operator $u \colon F \otimes E \to E \otimes F$, which we now specify.
Consider the group C*-algebra $\mathrm{C}^*(\mathbb{F}_2)$ of the free group on two generators.
Since $\mathrm{C}^*(\mathbb{F}_2)$ is separable we may pick a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space $H$ so that we get a unital and faithful $*$-representation $\mathrm{C}^*(\mathbb{F}_2) \subseteq {\mathcal{B}}(H)$.
 
Let the unitaries $W_2, W_3 \in {\mathcal{B}}(H)$ be the images of the free generators under this representation, and put $W_1 := I_H$ so that 
\[
\mathrm{C}^*(W_2, W_3) = \mathrm{C}^*(W_1,W_2, W_3) \simeq \mathrm{C}^*(\mathbb{F}_2).
\]
Set $E = F := H$ and define
\[
R := \tfrac{1}{\sqrt 3} \sum_{j=1}^3 W_j M_{h_j}^* \colon F \otimes E \to F.
\]
Since $M_{h_i}^* M_{h_j} = \delta_{i,j} {\operatorname{id}}_E$, we get $RR^* = {\operatorname{id}}_F$ and 
\[
R M_{h_j} = W_j/\sqrt{3}
\textup{ for }
j = 1,2,3.
\]
As $R$ is a co-isometry we have 
\[
\ker R = (1 - R^*R)(F \otimes E).
\]
The spaces $\ker R$ (which contains the ranges of $M_{h_j}$ for $j \geq 4$) and $(V F)^\perp$ (which contains the ranges of $L_{h_j}$ for $j \geq 2$) are separable and infinite-dimensional.
Choose a unitary 
\[
Z_0 \colon \ker R \to (VF)^\perp
\]
and extend it to a partial isometry
\[
Z \colon F \otimes E \to E \otimes F;\ Z|_{(\ker R)^\perp} = 0 \textup{ and } Z|_{\ker R} = Z_0.
\]
Hence $Z$ satisfies
\begin{align*}
Z^*Z = P_{\ker R} = {\operatorname{id}}_{F \otimes E} - R^*R & \quad\text{and}\quad
RZ^* = R Z^*ZZ^* = R ({\operatorname{id}}_{F \otimes E} - R^*R) Z^* = 0, \\
ZZ^* = P_{(VF)^\perp} = {\operatorname{id}}_{E \otimes F} - VV^* & \quad\text{and}\quad
Z^*V = Z^* Z Z^* V = Z^* ({\operatorname{id}}_{E \otimes F} - VV^*) V = 0.
\end{align*}
 
We now define the operator
\[
u := V R + Z \colon F \otimes E \to E \otimes F.
\]
On the one hand we have
\begin{align*}
u^*u 
& = (R^*V^* + Z^*)(VR + Z) 
= R^*V^*VR + R^*V^*Z + Z^*VR + Z^*Z \\
& = R^*R + 0 + 0 + ({\operatorname{id}}_{F \otimes E} - R^*R) = {\operatorname{id}}_{F \otimes E}.
\end{align*}
On the other hand we have
\begin{align*}
uu^*
& = (VR + Z) (R^*V^* + Z^*) 
= VRR^*V^* + VRZ^* + ZR^*V^* + ZZ^* \\
& = 
VV^* + 0 + 0 + ({\operatorname{id}}_{E \otimes F} - VV^*) = {\operatorname{id}}_{E \otimes F},
\end{align*}
and thus $u$ is a unitary.
 
Moreover we have $V^*u = V^*VR + V^*Z = R$, and applying this to \eqref{Eq:psi} we get
\[
\Psi(c_{ij})
= (V^* u M_{h_i}) (V^* u M_{h_j})^*
= (R M_{h_i}) (R M_{h_j})^*.
\]
For $i,j \in \{1,2,3\}$ we obtain
\[
\Psi(c_{ij}) = \frac{1}{3} W_i W_j^*.
\]
Since $W_1 = I_H$ and $\Psi$ is linear, we conclude that
\[
\Psi(3 c_{21}) = W_2 \quad\text{and}\quad \Psi(3 c_{31}) = W_3.
\]
Since $\Psi$ is a $*$-homomorphism it has closed range, and hence 
\[
\Psi(Q \mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast} Q) \supseteq \mathrm{C}^*(W_2,W_3) \simeq \mathrm{C}^*(\mathbb{F}_2),
\]
which is not exact, see \cite{Was76, Was78, Was90}.
As $\Psi$ is injective and exactness passes to C*-subalgebras, $\mathbf{K}_{{\mathbf{x}},\lambda_\ast}$ is not exact.
In particular, the Fock C*-algebra ${\mathcal{T}}_\lambda(X)$ is not exact, and hence also not nuclear, even though the coefficient C*-algebra $A=\mathbb{C}$ is nuclear.
 
In accordance with Theorem~\ref{T:faexact} and Theorem~\ref{T:fanuc}, the product system $X$ is not compactly aligned.
The element $(1,1)$ is the unique minimal common right multiple of $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$.
Since $u_{(1,0),(0,1)} = {\operatorname{id}}_{E \otimes F}$ and $u_{(0,1),(1,0)} = u$, we have
\[
i_{(1,0)}^{(1,1)}(\theta^E_{h_1,h_1}) = \theta^E_{h_1,h_1} \otimes {\operatorname{id}}_F = V V^*
\quad\text{and}\quad
i_{(0,1)}^{(1,1)}(\theta^F_{h_2,h_1}) = u M_{h_2} M_{h_1}^* u^*.
\]
Set 
\[
T := i_{(1,0)}^{(1,1)}(\theta^E_{h_1,h_1}) \, i_{(0,1)}^{(1,1)}(\theta^F_{h_2,h_1}).
\]
Using $V^* V = {\operatorname{id}}_F$, $V^* u = R$ and $R M_{h_j} = \frac{1}{\sqrt 3} W_j$, we obtain
\[
T V = V (R M_{h_2}) (R M_{h_1})^* = \tfrac{1}{3} V W_2 W_1^* = \tfrac{1}{3} V W_2.
\]
If $T \in {\mathcal{K}}(X_{(1,1)})$, then $T V \in {\mathcal{K}}(F, X_{(1,1)})$ and therefore
$(TV)^*(TV) \in {\mathcal{K}}(F)$.
However 
\[
(TV)^*(TV) = \frac{1}{9} W_2^* V^* V W_2 = \frac{1}{9} {\operatorname{id}}_F \notin {\mathcal{K}}(F),
\]
as $F$ is infinite-dimensional.
Hence $T \notin {\mathcal{K}}(X_{(1,1)})$, and so $X$ is not compactly aligned.
